\subsection{Purpose and reading rule}\label{purpose-and-reading-rule}

This supplement preserves the detailed source-by-source analysis removed
from the reader-facing edition of \emph{Finite Quantum Mechanics}. It
records original manuscript addresses, corrected statements,
counterexamples, implementation pointers, and unresolved obligations. A
file path, test name, successful build, or historical status label is
not itself a mathematical proof. The main paper states the current
results by their hypotheses and conclusions; this document records how
those results relate to the retained source manuscripts.

The source manuscripts referred to below are included under
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}
in the paper archive. They are historical inputs, not automatically
endorsed claims. Two public-record corrections prepared for author
submission are included under
\texttt{d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}/}.

\subsection{1. Evidence standards and historical claim
treatment}\label{evidence-standards-and-historical-claim-treatment}

The evidence obligation is determined by the statement's quantifiers. A
general mathematical statement requires an adequate written proof or a
formal proof of the same statement. A claim over a finite domain may
instead be settled by a complete exact enumeration, provided the domain
and enumeration are justified. An example test establishes only the
stated example.

Accordingly, each unresolved statement must receive one of the following
treatments:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  an adequate written proof;
\item
  a matching formal proof;
\item
  a complete exact finite argument appropriate to its quantifiers;
\item
  a restriction to the domain actually established;
\item
  an explicit statement that it remains open; or
\item
  withdrawal after a counterexample.
\end{enumerate}

File existence, compilation, schema validation, serialization, access
control, and a change of status label cannot decide whether this
obligation has been discharged. The repository maintains a historical
evidence register for reproduction, but its row counts and labels are
not a measure of mathematical progress and are not part of this
monograph's scientific summary.

The sixty-seven source manuscripts are preserved in the paper archive.
Six are redirect or alias stubs whose mathematical content is treated
with the destination result: residual density in §11.4, finite
realization in §11.6, the earlier phase selector in §11.27, and the
three packaging annexes QM\_064 (phase gauge, §11.28--§11.29), QM\_074
(no-signalling, §11.33--§11.34) and QM\_083 (complete positivity,
§11.38).

\subsection{2. Historical executable-model
note}\label{historical-executable-model-note}

\subsubsection{2.1 The executable model walk and its remaining
derivation
gap}\label{the-executable-model-walk-and-its-remaining-derivation-gap}

The historical claim that no executable model sequence existed is
refuted by the legacy integration tests. The deeper derivation problem
remains open: direct packet consumption does not derive the packet or
its quantum interpretation from primitive difference. The current test
is
\texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}E}.

The engines compute interferometer fringes, Sorkin cancellation,
rational Cayley isometries and PSD filtering under declared inputs. The
previous complete-walk test computed
\texttt{D\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})}
and then independently supplied its complexes, Cayley parameter,
cyclotomic weights and detector. The scalar difference did not construct
those inputs. The pairing fixture explicitly applies
\texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}q},
so its third-order cancellation is a consequence of the chosen quadratic
readout. The legacy cochain classifier is a numerical LP with a declared
tolerance; its output is not an exact certificate.

An exact control keeps the three-slit cochain carrier and amplitudes
fixed and varies only the readout. If each open slit contributes
amplitude \(1/3\), then \(P_2(S)=(|S|/3)^2\) and \(P_4(S)=(|S|/3)^4\)
are nonnegative, bounded by one, and have the same
empty\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}full endpoint values. Yet their
third-order terms are respectively \(0\) and \(4/9\). Even
\(P_1(S)=|S|/3\) has zero third-order term without being quadratic.
These are readout tables on the declared finite experiments, not
reconstructions of full operational theories. The proof, source audit
and native check are in the primitive\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}readout
boundary note
(\texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).
The later note
\texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
treats the phase-blind polynomial readouts \(\alpha|c|^2+\beta|c|^4\),
where the third-order term vanishes identically exactly when
\(\beta=0\); it does not treat general readouts.

\subsection{3. Publication provenance and public-record
obligations}\label{publication-provenance-and-public-record-obligations}

The paper archive contains all sixty-seven current original manuscripts
under
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/},
and every subsection 11.N of §4 gives the corresponding local address.
Historical hashes and per-source evidence observations remain in
repository custody records; the public
\texttt{S\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}S}
binds the exact copies shipped with this paper. The current repository
custody tests read all sixty-seven manuscripts: fifty-four match their
historical hashes and thirteen have separately pinned current
differences. The 2026-10-13 reconciliation permits current claim use,
including the five retained-copy comparisons described in §9, through
eighteen version comparisons across sixteen sources. Each assessment
identifies the current premise, supported conclusion, correction or
refusal, and affected claim rows. All historical hashes and dispositions
remain intact.

Repository custody also retains exact historical manuscript bytes for
the primitive-difference, superposition, channel-geometry,
Mermin--Peres, and finite-Hilbert-boundary papers. The affected versions
of the Born-normalization, interference, and later synthesis papers were
assessed independently for their declared current scope; unrecovered
historical bytes are not claimed equivalent to them. The omitted
placeholder sources contribute no mathematical construction. This
completes the current-use version assessment, not a replay of historical
Lean\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}Python receipts or closure of scientific
premise gaps. Published-version obligations and stale proof-receipt
scope remain separate.

\textbf{Publication status: sixty-five of the sixty-seven are
unpublished.} Established 2026-09-04 against
\texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
and confirmed by the author. Those sixty-five may be rewritten or
retired freely.

Retiring a package from this repository does not touch its public
record. \textbf{The two exceptions are the Born-normalization paper
(§11.11) and the channel-geometry paper (§11.35)}, each with a public
Zenodo deposit (\href{https://zenodo.org/records/20683775}{20683775} and
\href{https://zenodo.org/records/20550459}{20550459}). A rewrite of
either forks from the published record rather than replacing it, so the
relationship --- erratum, new version, or superseding paper --- must be
decided first. Repository custody tests record and enforce that
restriction.

The primitive-difference paper's header nevertheless read
\texttt{*\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}Z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{}*},
and fifty-seven others read
\texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D},
which in this tree means released-in-tree. That false header is treated
as a false receipt: a status line asserting a public record is a
receipt, and this one does not bind. The earlier retirement removed
those packages from the active corpus; restoring them does not validate
their headers. Those discrepancies remain provenance obligations, and
§11.1 records the correction.

The restored original, its copy under
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}
and the curated copy under
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}
now read
\texttt{U\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}E}
on that status line. The historical text that carried the false header
is pinned by its digest and its recovered version in
\texttt{c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}l};
it is evidence of the discrepancy, not a publication receipt.

The second drift is not cosmetic. In this tree's vocabulary
\emph{invariant} is a strictly stronger claim than \emph{compatible}, so
the public record may overclaim relative to the paper it names. Settle
which title the deposit carries before either is cited.

\subsection{4. Detailed constructions, corrections, and source
addresses}\label{detailed-constructions-corrections-and-source-addresses}

This section retains the historical subsection numbers so references
from the main paper remain stable. Placeholder-only subsections 11.13
and 11.44 and the source-note inventory formerly at 11.53 are omitted.
The remaining results are grouped by mathematical subject: finite
cochains and state-effect models (§§11.1--11.12), phase and dynamics
(§§11.14--11.29), composition, Bell inequalities, and channels
(§§11.30--11.38), operational interpretation and error thresholds
(§§11.39--11.47), gravity, contextuality, and the finite Hilbert
boundary (§§11.48--11.52), and synthesis (§§11.54--11.60). Each
subsection begins with a local link to the relevant original manuscript
in the paper archive. The link records provenance; the argument is the
stated object, hypotheses, proof or certificate, and counterexample in
the present text.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The source evaluated the quotient LP and the spectra numerically ``up
  to declared tolerance''. The implementation is exact:
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1} carries a
  replayed primal\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}dual certificate, and
  positivity is an exact inertia computation.
\item
  The cochain exponential
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{})}
  is implemented for integer cochains and a declared unit
  \texttt{u\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{})}
  of \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})}, so
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{})}
  exactly. The only roots of unity in
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})} are
  \texttt{±\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}±\allowbreak{}i}.
  For them, cochains that differ by the order on one edge collapse. Any
  other unit has infinite order, and the integer exponential is
  injective. Real-valued cochains and irrational scales are not covered.
\item
  The diagonal Gell-Mann scales
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{})}
  are irrational. Generators are stored as
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a}.
  Structure constants are exact surds
  \texttt{q\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})},
  and the Jacobi identity is checked as a rational identity after the
  common surd factor is removed.
\item
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y}'s
  connection Laplacian puts
  \texttt{-\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{})}
  in block
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{})}.
  That is the entrywise conjugate of the paper's
  \texttt{D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}A},
  which a test pins. For non-abelian fibres the same placement is not
  gauge covariant: with rational SO(3) fibres on a graph with two
  cycles, its characteristic polynomial changes under
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y}'s
  own gauge action, while
  \texttt{D\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}D}
  does not. That is a latent issue in
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y},
  not in this paper's U(1) setting.
\item
  The source's
  \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}Z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e}
  was false. Its earlier retirement did not correct that header. The
  status line now reads
  \texttt{U\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}E};
  the historical version remains evidence of the discrepancy, not a
  publication receipt.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} Continuum limits and physical model
selection. The phase scale, the edge weights and the
\texttt{S\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{})} label
space remain declared inputs, and no graph constructs the label space.
QMC-NC1 is still a scope fence. No quantum dynamics, Born rule, carrier
emergence or authority follows.

\subsubsection{11.2 A registry-relative quantum
interface}\label{a-registry-relative-quantum-interface}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Tower walk /
registry-relative interface lift

The paper's central statement is conditional: a failed commutative
representation forces a declared quantum interface only relative to a
declared lift registry, a valid transport, a resolving lift and
registry-relative minimality.
\texttt{t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r}
computes every part of that statement that has finite content. Three
registry verdicts are computed; the scalar and rotational rows fail by
declared witnesses, and the GPT and quaternionic rows are refused while
no composite rule is declared.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The paper's §11 registry block was an empty placeholder, and its O020,
  O021 and O022 prototypes were never vendored. The registry is now
  executable. The classical gluing row fails on an exhaustive search,
  the rebit row on the local-tomography count, and the complex row
  resolves only when its finite \texttt{M\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}2}
  obligations replay and its declared Born table has no defect.
\item
  A review found that the complex row resolved whenever the packet
  replayed, even when a declared Born probability differed from
  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{})}.
  Such a defect is an active closure failure. It now fails the row and
  removes
  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e},
  because an open obstruction dominates.
\item
  Three antecedents (lift protocol, admissibility, valid transport) are
  declared inputs of the canonical walk; they are not computed.
  \texttt{O\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m}
  and
  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e}
  are computed.
\item
  ``Registry-relative minimality'' is shown to be exactly that: adding
  one row with a declared composite rule removes uniqueness. When
  minimality has not been supplied, no unconditional forced-lift
  conclusion is emitted.
\item
  The package's only test,
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}y},
  compared a dict comprehension with the expression that built it. It
  retires with the package; the tests above replace it.
\item
  The O021 survival flags
  (\texttt{o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d},
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m},
  sealed terminal) are fields the validator has no path to set.
\item
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \text{CPTPMonotone} \nRightarrow \frac{1}{2}\|\cdot\|_1\)}\]
  is exhibited only by rescaling. That shows the normalization axiom is
  independent, and nothing more.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The six-role tower narrative, the survival
doctrine (C24--C26, still
\texttt{O\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N}), the cofiber
bridge (C31, see QM\_002) and every authority statement. The walk
derives no Hilbert space, Born rule or CPTP law. Those are imports of
the complex packet, and registry-relative minimality is not
comprehensive uniqueness.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The ``executable witness''
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e}
  was a pointer to code that did not exist. The witness now runs,
  together with the norm axioms the bridge relies on.
\item
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1} for a general
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}0} goes through the same certified path as the
  graph packets
  (\texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s}:
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s}
  proposes,
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l}
  replays). No second solver was written.
\item
  The type-separation refusal (C7) has a sharper witness than the Lean
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r}:
  equal scalars on the same ambient space and the same representative,
  with non-isomorphic cokernels.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The unrestricted
amplitude\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}composition bridge is not defined
until a realization functor is declared (C8). The
\texttt{(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})}-categorical
setting (C2) is not modelled. The theorem is a bridge, not an origin
statement, and it does not establish physical realization (C1, C10).

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Three of the five coherence-license fields are now computed rather
  than declared, and the observer basis is declared. The source's Lean
  took all five as booleans. The fifth, an internal policy flag, is not
  stored because it contributes no mathematical datum. A review found
  that a license or a lift checklist could be written by hand with every
  field true. Both now have private fields and come only from their
  evaluators, and the lift evaluator refuses negative coordinates.
\item
  The branch search is exact rational lexicographic descent with no
  tolerances. The \texttt{f\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}4} engine in
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}
  stays the production diagnostic and is not a claim source. A review
  found that the ranking followed the masses, which measure improvement
  in different coordinates and are not comparable across tiers. It now
  orders the candidates' points lexicographically.
\item
  The GOMC-06 ``universality'' companion and the
  GOMC-08A\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}09A countermodels imported Mathlib
  in the source. Here they are replaced by the exact countermodels
  above.
\item
  The report type contains no field for a physical conclusion. This is a
  software access restriction, not a theorem about observation or
  ontology.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The abstract thesis (004-C1) and the claim
that GOMC supersedes quantum formalism as Omega's base language
(004-C22) are interpretive, so they stay
\texttt{A\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D}
and
\texttt{U\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D}.
The stronger future representation target (003-C17) is still
\texttt{O\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N}. Physical QM does
not follow from GOMC (004-C23). The retired
\texttt{f\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}4} Plan002 surface (003-C16) is
untouched.

  The classifier's historical spellings
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s},

  and
  \texttt{O\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}
  map onto
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y}'s
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r},
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l}
  and
  \texttt{A\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e}.
  No new class enum was created.
\item
  With several Born entries, one gauge generator acts on every state and
  effect, and each entry contributes its own \texttt{d\allowbreak{}1}
  row. The identity
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
  holds row by row by trace cyclicity.
\item
  Membership in

  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a}'s
  exact row reduction. Separators come from its kernel basis of
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}T}.

  The Born-table refusal
  \texttt{I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}
  covers malformed entries only. A declared probability that disagrees
  with
  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{})}
  is a residual to classify, as the source's section PO-D19b (Born
  defect placement) requires, not a refusal.
\item
  The row typed
  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}L}
  (C10) was a parse artefact. It is the classifier's totality claim and
  is now evidenced as a computation.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The complex carrier, the Born pairing and
CPTP discipline are declared packet fields (C2). The classifier mints no
authority (C3, C5). Schema completeness does not show that the schema is
the only possible one (C7). Coefficient fields beyond
\texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})} are not
implemented.

\subsubsection{11.8 Hilbert-space cochains and
cohomology}\label{hilbert-space-cochains-and-cohomology}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Hilbert space cochains and
quantum cohomology
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper declared an adapter from a residual into a cochain complex and
a four-way admission rule for the residual it carries: exact, closed but
not exact, closure failure, or refused. It added a non-selection result:
classical and quantum realizations can land in the same class. The rule
now runs in
\texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n},
on top of

\textbf{What stays outside.} The architecture reading (C7) and the

phase, nonclassical composition, Born readout, channel transport,

targets PL-QM032-1 to 3 remain unmechanized.

\subsubsection{11.9 The state--effect
pairing}\label{the-stateeffect-pairing}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} State-effect pairing audit
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper grades candidate probability pairings on declared finite
packets by one set of checks and gives each a typed terminal. Its
headline is a non-result: the checks do not select the Born pairing.
\texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t}
now holds the audit, for any bilinear pairing or, as a nonlinear
control, a polynomial of the dot product. It builds the seven registry
rows on exact carriers and replays every check from the declared data.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The paper named carriers and checks but no samples. The states,
  effects, measurements, transports and joint tables are declared here
  on exact carriers, so each terminal replays explicit data. A different
  declaration could get a different terminal. The audit is
  registry-relative, as the paper says.
\item
  Checks 6 (quotient non-promotion) and 7 (finite replay) are not
  separate computations: every terminal is recomputed from its packet
  and says nothing beyond it. The scoped terminalizer
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}p}
  is not modelled, and no row is sealed.
\item
  The paper's non-selection witness was the arithmetic
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})}
  against
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{})}.
  The audit now puts a second pairing on the actual classical and Born
  packets, and it passes the whole skeleton, transport and gluing
  included. The finite checks cannot tell Born from Born composed with a
  Hadamard-symmetric channel. A further declared axiom, for example that
  a pure state gives probability 1 on its own projector, would.
\item
  The paper's body and ledger name the rebit terminal differently
  (``failed'' and ``conditional \ldots{} local tomography issue''). The
  audit reports
  \texttt{L\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\}}:
  the single-system checks pass, and the declared tensor composite fails
  local tomography.
\item
  The audit computes the product-effect rank from each row's own
  declared effects. An earlier version took the rank from
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}y}'s
  full bases, so a row could pass on numbers it did not earn; the
  complex packet then needed the \texttt{Y} basis, whose imaginary
  off-diagonal its other effects lack.
\item
  Quaternions enter through the standard complex representation
  \texttt{q\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}]\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}]\allowbreak{}]},
  so positivity is the crate's exact PSD decision on
  \texttt{4\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}4}
  complex matrices.
\item
  The Lean module
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}
  that the paper cites is not in this repository. C13 now rests on the
  exact countermodels above.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The proposed gluing theorems (C1) are prose
and are not mechanized here. The open conclusion in C9 has no
mathematical implementation in the crate. The downstream trace-norm and
interface audits (O025, O026) belong to their own papers.

\subsubsection{11.10 Density matrices as diagonal residual
weights}\label{density-matrices-as-diagonal-residual-weights}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Density matrices as
diagonal residual weights
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper read a finite residual-weight distribution as a diagonal
density: it is a state, its purity
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2}
is one exactly on one sector, and coherence is a lift the weights do not
force. QM\_003's
\texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s}
already held the ledger, the diagonal density and the purity. The
paper's own statements are now checked against it.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  No new module was needed: the ledger, density and purity were
  QM\_003's code. This paper's rows now cite tests of their own
  statements.
\item
  The theorem was cited as mechanized in
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y}
  (ENC-1126). That Lean file is not in this repository, and
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n}
  in
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}
  is a different, two-level module. C5 is recorded as
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N}:
  an exhaustive check on declared ledgers, with the general statement
  proved in prose.
\item
  The basis-relativity row (C9) was interpretive. It now has a computed
  witness, and the same witness separates the purity of the state from
  the purity of its diagonal.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The descent from sector populations (C2),
the nonclaims (C10) and the firewall (C11) are fences. Channel dynamics
on the density (rung 4) belong to the channels papers.

\subsubsection{11.11 Born normalization and the conditional Hilbert
lift}\label{born-normalization-and-the-conditional-hilbert-lift}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Conditional Hilbert lifts
and Born normalization redundancy
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper separated three things: normalizing sector weights, which
already gives a unit-sum profile; lifting them to amplitudes
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{})},
which returns the same profile; and uniqueness of the quadratic rule,
which needs Gleason's imported hypotheses. Most of its theorems land on
modules that already existed. The new piece is
\texttt{p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w},
which replaces the paper's Monte Carlo phase average with an exact
average over a declared finite phase group.

\subsubsection{11.12 Measurement update as idempotent
conditioning}\label{measurement-update-as-idempotent-conditioning}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Selective measurement
update as idempotent conditioning
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper cast a selective measurement on finite outcome weights as
conditioning on a declared outcome sector: keep the sector and
renormalize. It proved in prose that the update collapses, is
idempotent, is repeatable, and reads the sector's share as its
probability, and it fenced off within-sector coherence and incompatible
measurements. The crate's
\texttt{m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e}
computes the Lüders rule in floating point.
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g}
now does both exactly, and the exact Lüders update makes the two fences
concrete.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The theorem was proved in prose, with Lean only targeted. It is now
  checked exhaustively on declared ledgers and sectors. The general
  statement stays prose-proved, and no Lean was written.
\item
  The paper said its update is the Lüders rule specialized to outcome
  weights. The specialization is now a computed agreement on diagonal
  densities, and the exact Lüders update shows what the specialization
  drops.
\item
  The existing
  \texttt{m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e}
  module works in floating point. The exact update here does not replace
  it.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The measurement problem, the projection
postulate as ontology and preferred-basis selection (C10) are not
addressed; the fence now has a computed witness for coherence. The
descent from a measured state (C2) and the firewall (C11) are fences.

\subsubsection{11.14 Finite weighted transport
calculus}\label{finite-weighted-transport-calculus}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Finite weighted transport
calculus
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper proposed a finite weighted transport calculus: histories on a
finite graph weighted in a commutative semiring, coupled to a cochain
layer that carries phase and closure. Its finite kernels now compute
exactly: graded path-sums and their transfer matrices over five
semirings, the split-point overcount of the ungraded free category,
cancellation, and phase as a gauge-triviality obstruction decided with a
witness.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  ``3:1'' is the count for one path of length two. In general the
  ungraded split sum counts each path once per split point,
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \sum_\gamma (|\gamma|+1)w(\gamma)\)}\],
  which is no fixed multiple of \texttt{Z} once paths of different
  lengths meet.
\item
  T2's ring hypothesis is not needed for the finite transfer identity,
  which holds over Boolean and nonnegative weights. Subtraction is
  needed only to form a generator.
\item
  T3's ``\texttt{w} gauge-trivial iff \texttt{a} is a coboundary'' holds
  for integer cochains under a declared unit of infinite order. Under a
  unit of order \texttt{n}, a cochain whose cycle sums are multiples of
  \texttt{n} is pure gauge without being a coboundary. For real-valued
  \texttt{a} the equivalence holds only modulo
  \texttt{2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}Z},
  which is not implemented. The cocycle hypothesis
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
  carries weight: on a filled triangle the same flux is curvature, not
  an \texttt{H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1} class.
\item
  The Boolean and nonnegative semirings are zero-sum-free: a sum can
  vanish only if every summand vanishes. They also have no zero
  divisors, so a path weight vanishes only when some edge weight
  vanishes. These are separate additive and multiplicative hypotheses,
  not consequences of one another.
\item
  The Rust
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l}
  was never vendored. The checks it was meant to run are
  \texttt{g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m},
  \texttt{u\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y}
  and QM\_000's
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t}.
  \texttt{S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n}
  (ENC-1069) is not in the tree, so the Lean half of C27 has no
  evidence. No function here maps weights to probabilities, so there is
  no ``Born refusal'' to implement.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} C1, C2, C5, C8, C11, C16, C18, C19, C21,
C23 and C24 are fences or synthesis prose. C7, the
\texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{})}
flow and
\texttt{H\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}T},
stays a refusal; its finite witnesses are in QM\_034 and QM\_035. Born
terminalization and pairing non-uniqueness (C12, C13) belong to the
state--effect pairing audit, the trace-norm firewall (C14) to the
norm-selection papers, and C22 collects results owned by other papers
(the rebit
\texttt{9\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0}
count is
\texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}y}).
C15 names an external decision procedure, which is not in this crate;
C17 is doctrine with no finite content. The dagger-compact comparison
and the uniqueness of the host stay open.

\subsubsection{11.15 Finite path sums as graded
transport}\label{finite-path-sums-as-graded-transport}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Finite path-sum as graded
transport
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper split a sum over histories into a graded skeleton (matrix
powers), a phase lift (interference) and an imported continuum, and took
a position that quantum probability is L1 normalization. The skeleton
and the finite facts under the position now compute exactly; the
continuum and the framing stay outside.

The paper admitted a continuum path integral only as the certified limit
of finite time-sliced shadows. The finite shadow now replays exactly:
histories are enumerated once each, actions are exact rationals, and the

is an exact object rather than a decimal. Comparing shadows exactly
shows that the paper's own free-particle family is torn by refinement.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{})}

  \texttt{2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}i}
  is not reproduced.

  the source's \texttt{-\allowbreak{}2} charges \texttt{i} on both

  The refinement-compatibility hypothesis of part (ii) fails for the
  paper's first target: on a finite carrier the free-particle kernel
  changes with the partition, and no declared normalization closes the

  The implementation sketch's
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l}
  value is replaced by

  (\texttt{Q\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w},

\subsubsection{11.17 Discrete Schrödinger cochain
transport}\label{discrete-schruxf6dinger-cochain-transport}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Discrete Schrödinger
cochain transport
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper stated the continuous-time Schrödinger equation on a finite
graph, norm conservation for Hermitian \texttt{H}, and a holonomy
obstruction. The finite content now computes exactly: the instantaneous
norm rate, an exactly unitary and a non-unitary finite step, and
holonomy as the invariant that local data miss. The claim ledger has no
QM\_033 rows, so the table uses the paper's own claim IDs.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  C2 is a statement about continuous time. Its exact finite content is
  that the rate vanishes for Hermitian \texttt{H}, and that conservation
  then depends on the step: the Cayley (Crank--Nicolson) step conserves
  the norm exactly for every rational
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u}, and the explicit step
  conserves it only on
  \texttt{k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}H}.
\item
  The ``\(L^1\) probability mass'' is \(\sum_v|\psi_v|^2\): the \(L^1\)
  norm of
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2},
  which is the squared \texttt{L\allowbreak{}2} norm of
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i}.
\item
  C3's
  ``\texttt{T\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{})}
  is non-zero whenever
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{};\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}''
  is false: nonzero
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1} allows a
  nontrivial holonomy but does not force one. What holds is gauge
  invariance of the cycle product, and that vertex terms and hopping
  moduli do not fix the unitary class. The angle sum
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}H}
  is transcendental; the exact invariant is the cycle product itself.
\item
  The discrete Hamiltonian is QM\_000's connection Laplacian
  \texttt{D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}A}.
\item
  The Lean targets the paper names are not Lake modules;
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}
  holds Lean text for a two-state swap.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} C1, the equation
\texttt{i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i}
itself, and C4, the lift to
\texttt{L\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{})}:
continuous time, the exponential
\texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{})}
and continuum limits are not computed.

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Matrix and
differential-equation representations
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The package is named for matrix versus differential-equation
representation, but its text makes a narrower point. In the
\texttt{3\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3}
Gaussian-integer matrices, the first three Gell-Mann matrices have trace
zero while their commutators do not vanish, so a trace readout cannot
see noncommutativity. Everything in the paper is closed arithmetic on
named matrices. It now runs on the crate's Gell-Mann basis of
\texttt{C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}3} rather than on a
second copy of the matrices, and the single witness is extended to all
28 pairs of that basis. The claim ledger has no QM\_040 rows, so the
table uses the paper's own claim IDs.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The carrier
  \texttt{Z\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}]\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{})}
  sits inside the crate's exact
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})} matrices. The
  paper's
  \texttt{L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}1},
  \texttt{L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}2},
  \texttt{L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}3}
  are the unscaled shapes of the first three generators of
  \texttt{g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s},
  so no second copy of the matrices was written.
\item
  The paper declined to construct all eight SU(3) generators; the crate
  already has them. The census over the 28 pairs replaces the single
  witness: the trace readout is zero on every pair, so it cannot
  separate the 3 commuting pairs from the 25 others. The trace of a
  commutator is always zero, so no trace readout of the bracket helps
  either.
\item
  The twelve cited declarations
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}*}
  are not in the Lake workspace
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}.
  Their text survives as Markdown in
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}.
  The
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}2}
  binding was not checked.
\item
  The package name promises a comparison of matrix and
  differential-equation representations that the text never makes. The
  finite comparison of the Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures is under
  QM\_041.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} C1 (the carrier) is a definition and C6
(the authority predicate) a scope fence. Physical locality or colour,
SU(N) representation theory, Hermitian dynamics and any continuum
reading are not treated.

\subsubsection{11.21 Heisenberg-picture evolution and history
decoherence}\label{heisenberg-picture-evolution-and-history-decoherence}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Heisenberg-picture model
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper made three statements: the Gell-Mann--Hartle decoherence
matrix
\texttt{D\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{})}
has a nonnegative diagonal equal to the path probabilities; vanishing
off-diagonal entries give probability additivity; and the
Heisenberg-picture observable
\texttt{A\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{})}
obeys
\texttt{d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}]}.
The first two now compute exactly in
\texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l},
on class operators built from Heisenberg-picture projectors. The third
has the wrong sign for the paper's own
\texttt{U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{})}. Its exact finite
content, the Schrödinger--Heisenberg duality of declared steps and the
derivative of the Cayley path, is computed in
\texttt{h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e}.

& a second qubit that records the first outcome through a CNOT makes

and all 15 coarse-grainings of the four histories obey the sum rule;
without the record the pair
