\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o} was ``the discrete
  \texttt{L\allowbreak{}1} diagonal density''. The diagonal of
  \texttt{D} equals the classical path mass only for fine-grained
  histories whose first projection is in the eigenbasis of a diagonal
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o}. For coarse-grained histories
  it is a Born weight and differs from the path masses by the
  interference term. Nonnegativity needs
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0},
  and then \texttt{D} is positive semidefinite, which is more than the
  paper claimed.
\item
  Projectors that all commute, as diagonal projectors with no dynamics
  between them do, make every family decohere trivially. The decoherent
  example here is the standard one: a record kept in a second system.
\item
  Additivity under every coarse-graining holds exactly when
  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
  for
  \texttt{j\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}k}.
  Vanishing \texttt{D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}k} is
  sufficient, not necessary; the complex family above is the
  countermodel. The paper's
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}|}
  needs square roots; only its vanishing is used, and that is decided
  entrywise. It is not an
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l}
  functional.
\item
  C3 is off by a sign. With the paper's
  \texttt{U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{})},
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}]};
  with
  \texttt{U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{})}
  the paper's formula holds. No exponential is computed. The derivative
  is taken exactly, with first-order jets of the rational Cayley path,
  at rational points. The ledger row \nolinkurl{QM_041-C3} is now
  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N},
  citing the sign test and the failure of finite steps away from
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0};
  the corrected statement is the one in the table, and it is recorded
  here rather than in the ledger.
\item
  C1 and C2 are now
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N}
  with the scopes above: C1 needs
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
  and holds as ``path probability'' only for fine-grained histories, and
  C2 is sufficient, not necessary.
\item
  The Cayley steps are not a one-parameter group in the additive
  parameter. The composite and rate generator need not be scalar
  multiples of the original generator; the sufficient spectral condition
  and exceptional parameters are recorded in QM\_035.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} C4, the quarantine of infinite history
spaces and master equations, is a scope fence. Continuous time,
\texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{})}
and master equations are not computed.

residual}\label{a-two-history-decoherence-residual}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Gell-Mann--Hartle cochain
decoherence
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper kept the complex decoherence functional as imported context
and proved one integer identity: for a triple
\texttt{(\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})},
the global weight minus the local diagonal weight is
\texttt{2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2}. The
functional itself now computes in
\texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l},
and the identity turns out to concern the real part: for complex entries
the residual is
\texttt{2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2}.
The two conditional standard facts, positivity and normalization, are
computed together with the failure of each hypothesis. The claim ledger
has no QM\_043 rows, so the table uses the paper's own claim IDs.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}

  makes
  ``\texttt{d\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
  implies global \texttt{!\allowbreak{}=} local'' false, with the

  and residual 0. Read as

\item

\textbf{What stays outside.} C5, persistence of a phase class under a
map on
\texttt{H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{};\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{})},
stays \texttt{O\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N}: the paper
declares no map. For a declared map on a declared graph, persistence is
the gauge-equivalence decision that
\texttt{h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}
already makes (QM\_063). No probability is assigned to a family that
breaks a sum rule.

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Dirac equation admission
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

QM\_050 was a reserved slot with one placeholder row (QM\_050-C0) and no
text. Its topic, admitting the Dirac equation on a finite exact carrier,
is now computed in two modules.
\texttt{d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}

momenta, its solutions, its adjoint structure and the spin elements that
act on it.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  There was no source text. The implementation is limited to what a
  finite exact carrier decides: algebraic admission of the gamma
  matrices, plane-wave solutions at rational momenta, and the lattice
  operator on declared periodic lattices.
\item
  A rotation or boost is never given by an angle or a rapidity. Spin
  elements are declared by rational half-parameters, and a rational
  boost whose half-rapidity is irrational is refused with its square
  class rather than approximated.
\item
  The crate's canonical rational boost \texttt{B\allowbreak{}1} in
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t}
  has no spin lift with entries in
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})}: its Doppler
  factor
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2}
  is not a square there. Its square, with Doppler factor 4, lifts. The
  refusal is relative to the field: over
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{})},
  which contains
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2},
  \texttt{B\allowbreak{}1} lifts exactly.
\item
  The lattice counts are the finite form of fermion doubling on the
  declared lattices, and the Wilson term trades the doublers for chiral
  symmetry there. The Nielsen--Ninomiya theorem itself is not proved.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The Dirac equation in position space on a
continuum, the Dirac sea and quantum field theory, spin lifts of
rational Lorentz transformations other than plane boosts and rotations,
and any continuum limit of the lattice operator. \nolinkurl{QM_050-C0}
remains a reserved-slot definition.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  There was no source text. ``Spinor structure'' is implemented in its
  two finite senses: lifting single rotations through the double cover,
  and lifting a flat transport on a finite complex.
\item
  Rotations are declared by rational matrices; no angle is formed. A
  lift is exact or refused. The obstruction for one rotation is its
  spinor norm, the squarefree part of the norm of its Euler--Rodrigues
  vector, computed with
  \texttt{q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d}.
\item
  For a transport the obstruction is a face cochain over
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}2}: a flat lift exists exactly
  when it equals the traversal parities of some sign change. That is
  decided by exhaustive search over the
  \texttt{2\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}E} sign changes
  and checked against ranks over
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}2}. The class counts 4, 4, 2 and
  1 are compared with the order of
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{};\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})},
  computed independently, for the torus, the Klein bottle, the
  projective plane and the sphere. That the two always agree (the flat
  lifts form a torsor over
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{};\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})})
  is checked on these complexes, not proved.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} Spin structures on smooth manifolds,
Stiefel--Whitney classes as characteristic classes,
\texttt{S\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{})}
for \texttt{n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3},
and transports whose edge rotations have no rational lift, which are
refused rather than lifted over a quadratic field. \nolinkurl{QM_051-C0}
remains a reserved-slot definition.

\subsubsection{11.25 Superposition as a quotient
fiber}\label{superposition-as-a-quotient-fiber}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Superposition as the
quotient fiber
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper placed the phase content of a superposition in the fiber of
the phase-blind projection \(\pi(c)_g=|c_g|^2/\sum_h|c_h|^2\) over a
declared sector basis: invisible to the diagonal readout, visible after
a mixing map. The projection, its fibers and the descent question now
compute exactly over
\texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})}. Two statements had
to be corrected. The descent criterion holds only when the zero vector
is kept as a point of the quotient, and not every rational simplex point
is a quotient point.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The source stated that a linear map descends through the quotient
  exactly when it has at most one nonzero entry per row. For the
  projection defined on nonzero vectors only, this is false:
  \texttt{[\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}]\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}]\allowbreak{}]}
  sends every configuration it does not annihilate to
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})},
  so it descends to a constant. The criterion holds once the zero vector
  is a separate point. Then a row with nonzero entries
  \texttt{m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}k}
  is refused with the pair
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}k}
  and
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}k}:
  they are phase equivalent, and the row annihilates the first but not
  the second. The source's stress suite raised an error on exactly this
  case,
  \texttt{[\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}]\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}]\allowbreak{}]}.
\item
  The source took the quotient base to be the rational simplex. A point
  \texttt{p} has a preimage in
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}n}
  only when each product
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h}
  of nonzero coordinates is a sum of two rational squares, and a real
  rational preimage only when each is a rational square. So
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{})}
  is not a quotient point, and a lift
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{})}
  need not exist in the declared carrier.
\item
  The source enumerated a ``discrete fiber'' from the base point itself,
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}±\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{})}.
  That vector lies over \texttt{p} only when the nonzero weights are
  equal:
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{})}
  projects to
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{})}.
  The port enumerates through a declared representative and a declared
  finite unit group.
\item
  Amplitudes are Gaussian rationals rather than real rationals. Where
  the source answered ``not equivalent'' for zero vectors and length
  mismatches, the port refuses with a typed error; floating-point input
  cannot be represented.
\item
  The package's Lean modules
  (\texttt{G\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l},
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n},
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r},
  \texttt{M\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n})
  prove the two-sector witness and the non-descent of the Hadamard map.
  They now live in
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}
  as roots of its library, next to the overlapping
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n},
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}
  and
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}.
  A Mathlib-free staging build with toolchain
  \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1}
  compiled them without
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y};
  the only axiom reported is
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d},
  in
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}.
  That is a build, not a receipted replay.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} QM-060-C8 and C9 remain fences: nothing
here derives Hilbert space, unitarity or the Born rule. The quadratic
readout, the sector basis and the phase groups stay declared. The
continuous relative-phase torus
\texttt{U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})}
is not constructed; only rational points of the circle and the finite
groups \texttt{\{\allowbreak{}±\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\}} and
\texttt{\{\allowbreak{}±\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}±\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}\}}
are used. The monopolar half of the descent criterion is checked on
declared maps and configurations; its general argument is prose.

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{11.26 Interference beyond \(L^1\)
weights}{11.26 Interference beyond L\^{}1 weights}}\label{interference-beyond-l1-weights}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Interference as the
non-\(L^1\) resource
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper had two parts. Part A re-packaged an earlier result: the
interfered weight \(I(c)=|\sum_s c_s|^2\) is not a function of the
diagonal weights
\texttt{|\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2},
and a primitive-difference phase has no holonomy. Part B defined a
buildability set \texttt{S} of four conditions on a declared
architecture. Part A now computes exactly over
\texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})}, and the
non-identifiability is sharpened to a characterization. Part B is small:
apart from the race condition it is a definition.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The source's engine called
  \texttt{D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2}
  the non-L1 resource deficit, and its mutation audit tied
  \texttt{S\allowbreak{}4} to
  \texttt{D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}.
  \texttt{D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a}
  depends only on the
  \texttt{|\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}|},
  so it is a function of the diagonal weights:
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})} and
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})}
  have the same
  \texttt{D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2}
  and opposite cross terms \texttt{±\allowbreak{}2}. It is the largest
  cross term among the sign changes of \texttt{v} (checked over every
  sign pattern of 40 generated vectors), a bound on the interference
  rather than the part the diagonal misses. It is kept as
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t}
  with its exact identities: invariance under all 552 signed
  permutations tested, the disjoint and sign-aligned superadditivity
  formulas,
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})}
  on the uniform vector, and the normalized form, which is the
  l1-coherence of the normalized state.
\item
  A1 is sharpened. On a fiber of the diagonal layer, \texttt{I} is
  constant exactly when the support has one point: with two nonzero
  coordinates, multiplying one of them by \texttt{-\allowbreak{}1} or by
  \texttt{i} changes \texttt{I}.
\item
  \texttt{S\allowbreak{}4} is computed rather than declared: an
  architecture carries a U(1) connection on a finite carrier, and
  \texttt{S\allowbreak{}4} holds when that connection is not gauge
  trivial. \texttt{S\allowbreak{}3} stays a declared boolean; no
  Lieb--Robinson cone is computed. The rates are exact rationals. The
  only non-definitional content of B1 is that
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}0}
  for every \texttt{n} exactly when
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}.
\item
  The source's summary said that the four conditions are necessary and
  sufficient for computational advantage and partition finite
  architectures into classical and non-classical ones. Nothing computes
  advantage or simulability; \texttt{S} is a conjunction of predicates
  on declared data.
\item
  C8 read the interference resource as non-coboundary holonomy and said
  the cross term was not yet a closed-form function of the holonomy.
  Over unit Gaussian rationals it is: for walks with a common source and
  sink,
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle I-\sum_p w_p=2\sum_{p<q}\sqrt{w_pw_q}\operatorname{Re}(H(p)\overline{H(q)})\)}\]
  (QM\_063). A gauge-trivial connection does not give zero interference.
  It makes every relative holonomy one and \(I=(\sum_p\sqrt{w_p})^2\),
  again a function of the weights. The row stays interpretive.
\item
  The ledger's evidence for C5, C6, C7, C12, C13 and C14 named test
  classes that the package does not contain
  (\texttt{T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e},
  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x},
  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s}),
  and the package's mutation audit describes twelve mutations that do
  not match its test file.
\item
  The package's Lean modules
  (\texttt{I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t},
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y},
  \texttt{B\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S})
  now live in
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}.
  Its
  \texttt{G\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n}
  duplicated QM\_060's apart from a header comment, so the two were
  merged into one module. All of them compiled without
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y} in
  the same staging build as QM\_060's; that is a build, not a receipted
  replay.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} QM-061-C9 (the complex phase carrier is
imported), C10, C11, C15 and C17 remain definitions and fences. C8 and
C16 (threshold theorems read as \texttt{S}-witnesses, the make-or-break
read as
\texttt{S\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}∩\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}4})
stay interpretive. Nothing here says that any device satisfies
\texttt{S}, and no link between \texttt{S\allowbreak{}4} and classical
simulability is computed.

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{11.27 Selecting a \(U(1)\) phase
structure}{11.27 Selecting a U(1) phase structure}}\label{selecting-a-u1-phase-structure}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} The \(U(1)\) selector
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper proposes a conditional complex-carrier selector. Its verified
finite content is narrower: among the two field automorphisms of
\texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})}, phase invariance
of the specified pairing selects conjugation; a real rotation generator
can supply a declared complex structure
\texttt{J\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}I}.
Comparing the sign group with the full quaternion unit group does not
classify every phase realization: quaternions contain abelian circle
subgroups too. A Frobenius-based selection must separately assume a
finite-dimensional associative real division algebra and require its
whole unit-norm group, rather than an available subgroup, to be the
phases. Continuity, real scalar structure and operational availability
are additional premises; no unconditional selection of \texttt{C} or
\texttt{U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})} follows.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The cited Layer-1 model is a toy over the integers, with the ``phase''
  \texttt{u\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2} and
  a slot factor \texttt{u\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2}.
  Here the phases are unit Gaussian rationals and the pairing is built
  from a field automorphism of
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})}; since
  \texttt{x\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}1}
  has only the roots \texttt{±\allowbreak{}i}, the identity and
  conjugation are all of them.
\item
  The cited witness that \texttt{C} admits an abelian, order-unbounded
  phase group is the product
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}Z\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})}.
  That product is not \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}Z}: it is
  uncountable and contains infinite-order elements, whereas
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}Z} is a countable torsion group.
  Roots of unity in \texttt{U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})}
  form \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}Z}; obtaining them uses a
  compatible direct-limit system, not this product. The unit circle of
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})} has torsion
  \texttt{\{\allowbreak{}±\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}±\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}\}}
  only, and no number field contains roots of unity of every order. What
  is computed is the order-by-order statement for the cyclotomic fields
  in the crate.
\item
  The quaternion group is generated by closure from two Gaussian
  matrices instead of being given as a multiplication table.
\item
  The paper had no code or Lean package. The Lean files it cited,
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}
  and
  \texttt{U\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r},
  survive only as text under
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/}.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} QM-062-C1 and C11 remain fences; C1's
finite content, that a sign-valued carrier already interferes, is
computed under QM\_060 and QM\_061. C8, the conditional forcing, stays
interpretive, and C9 and C10 (continuity of reversible dynamics; field
uniqueness across dimensions) stay imports. No continuous
\texttt{S\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})} or
\texttt{U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})} is constructed. The
dual-alias stub QM\_028 is absorbed into this entry.

(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

and derived what follows under it: two-path interference is controlled
by the relative loop holonomy, holonomy and intensity are gauge
invariant, every connection on a tree is gauge trivial, face curvature
is gauge invariant, and a flat connection can keep global holonomy. All
of it now computes exactly over unit Gaussian rationals. Amplitudes
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{})}
are formed only for weights that are rational squares.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The source took real weights and phases in
  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}Z}.
  Here transports take values in the unit Gaussian rationals, a dense
  subgroup of \texttt{U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})}, and
  a weight with an irrational square root is refused rather than
  approximated, as in
  \texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g}.
  The two-path identity is then an equality of rationals, and
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{})}
  is the real part of the face holonomy.
\item
  The source derived Corollary 4.4 from the imported classification
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{};\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}Z\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{})}.
  What is computed is finite: a connection is gauge trivial exactly when
  its spanning-forest residual is 1, the residual classes of
  quarter-turn connections are counted exhaustively, and the verdict
  never reports a flat nontrivial connection on the filled square.
\item
  The executable target QC-SUP-PL4 asked a verifier to reject
  inconsistent reverse-edge transport, endpoint mismatches and
  gauge-equivalence claims with unequal loop holonomy. Reverse transport
  is conjugation by construction, so it cannot be declared
  inconsistently; endpoint mismatches, irrational weights, and
  connections or walks from another carrier are refused;
  \texttt{g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}
  returns \texttt{N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e} when the
  residuals differ. A review found that a walk from another carrier was
  refused only when it named an edge the carrier lacks; a walk that fit
  the edge count was accepted, and
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p}
  could panic on it. A walk must now replay on the carrier
  (\texttt{O\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}),
  in
  \texttt{h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e}
  and in
  \texttt{U\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y}.
\item
  The paper had no code or Lean package; its mechanization section
  listed targets only. The packaging annex QM\_064 is absorbed into this
  entry.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} QCS-C9 (higher-form holonomy) stays refused
and QCS-C10 stays a fence. QCS-C11, that the trace of a matrix-valued
SU(2) relative holonomy lower-bounds separability defects, is a
conjecture without a defined defect and is not implemented. Nothing here
derives the U(1) carrier, the square root or the quadratic readout;
graphs and 2-complexes stay declared carriers.

\subsubsection{11.30 Product non-factorization in bipartite
systems}\label{product-non-factorization-in-bipartite-systems}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Product non-factorization
as a bipartite obstruction
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper defined the product defect of a finite joint weight table,
\texttt{d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}W},
and its \texttt{l\allowbreak{}1} mass. It stated that the mass vanishes
exactly on tables that factor, and that the mass is blind to
entanglement. Both now compute exactly. Factorization is decided
separately, through
\texttt{2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2}
minors, so the equivalence compares two independent computations. The
entanglement firewall is an explicit countermodel.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The source called the mass \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i} and
  read the equivalence classes of equal defect as a quotient
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d}
  with the mass as its gauge. The mass is the raw
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}1} norm of a nonlinear defect. It is named
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s}.
  It is not the quotient mass
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1} of
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l},
  and it is not the \texttt{l\allowbreak{}1} distance to the set of
  product tables:
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{})}
  is at distance
  \texttt{2\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}5}
  from the diagonal-half table, whose mass is 1. It is the distance to
  the product of the table's own marginals, twice the total-variation
  distance when
  \texttt{W\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1}.
\item
  The source declined to claim that the mass is monotone under local
  stochastic maps. For one product map
  \texttt{g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}B}
  it is. The marginals of the image are
  \texttt{g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}A}
  and
  \texttt{g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}B},
  so the defect of the image is
  \texttt{g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}B}
  applied to the defect, and a stochastic map does not increase
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}1} mass. The tests check instances; the argument
  is prose. Under a mixture of product maps (shared randomness) the mass
  can rise from 0.
\item
  The entangled side of the countermodel is certified relative to all
  product states, not by a separate policy:
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}|}
  is PSD, so
  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}Q\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
  for every product state, and
  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2}.
\item
  The descent accepts any declared local orthogonal bases, unnormalised,
  so Hadamard-basis tables stay rational.
\item
  A review found two unchecked inputs.
  \texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p}
  has public fields, so a hand-built map with no target states or short
  rows made the local-map action panic or drop weight; the action now
  re-checks that each map is row-stochastic. And the witness certified
  ``entanglement'' for any Hermitian operator that paired negatively,
  such as \texttt{-\allowbreak{}I}; certification now requires a state,
  while
  \texttt{v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}e}
  stays the linear pairing.
\item
  The cited Lean module
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}
  (ENC-1123) is not in
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/},
  and the ledger already recorded no surviving evidence. The Rust checks
  replace it. C5 is a finite computation, not a proof of the general
  statement. The package's notebook imports a library that the package
  does not contain.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} QM-070-C10 (the firewall and authority
fence) and QM-070-C12 (the falsifiability statement) remain fences.
QM-070-C11 stays interpretive; mutual information and Kullback--Leibler
divergence are not computed. Multipartite gluing is not addressed, and
the product basis remains a declaration.

\subsubsection{11.31 Entanglement as failure of
separability}\label{entanglement-as-failure-of-separability}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Entanglement as a
separability obstruction
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper proved witness soundness relative to a declared finite family
of product states: a functional that is at least \texttt{t} on every
member and below \texttt{t} on \texttt{w} shows that \texttt{w} is not a
convex combination of members. It kept completeness out of scope. Both
directions now compute. For a finite family, completeness is finite
linear-programming duality. Every vector receives either a verified
convex decomposition or a verified separating functional. The linear
program is solved by
\texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s}
and replayed by
\texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l}.
The two-qubit density-matrix case that the paper listed as open is also
computed.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The source called completeness ``the expensive half''. Relative to a
  finite declared family it is not. The decision solves
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \min_\lambda 2|1-\sum_k\lambda_k|+2\|w-P\lambda\|_1+\|\lambda\|_1\)}\].
  Its value is at least one plus the constraint residual, with value
  exactly one on members. At value one the minimiser is a decomposition.
  Above one the replayed dual
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{})}
  gives the witness
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}P},
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1},
  with gap equal to the value minus one. Completeness over all product
  states, which are not a finite family, is not computed.
\item
  The paper's worked example separates
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})}
  with
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{})}.
  The cited Lean witness
  \texttt{z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}
  separates the zero vector from the unit vectors. Both are checked.
\item
  The paper listed the density-matrix instantiation as an open target.
  Real coordinates of Hermitian operators make two-qubit states vectors,
  so the declared-family decision applies to them. Relative to all
  product states, the Bell state is certified by the decomposable
  witness of QM\_070's entry. PPT is necessary for separability. Its
  sufficiency on
  \texttt{2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2}
  carriers, the Peres--Horodecki criterion, is cited as an imported
  theorem and not computed.
\item
  ``\texttt{P}-nonseparable'' is relative to the declared family, and a
  separable state can be \texttt{P}-nonseparable. The C10 countermodel
  exhibits one.
\item
  The source described the obstruction mass as the distance from
  \texttt{w} to
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{})}.
  That distance is not computed. The gap of a decided witness is a
  certified margin, not the distance.
\item
  The cited Lean module
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}
  (ENC-1124) is not in
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/}.
  The Rust checks replace it.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} General separability over the continuum of
product states, multipartite structure, and entanglement measures.
QM-071-C11 remains a fence. QM-071-C12 stays interpretive; its CHSH
instance is computed in QM\_073's entry. QM-071-C1 and C2 remain
definitions, and the product family is always a declaration.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The least-ness of the triangle was proposed but not proved. It is now
  decided for simple graphs on up to four vertices. It depends on the
  carrier convention: if two edges may join the same pair of loci, a
  digon already carries a pattern that no family removes. The general
  statement follows from
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})}
  over \texttt{F\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}2}: every pattern is
  removable on a forest, and some pattern is not removable on a graph
  with a cycle. The tests compare it on all small graphs with a
  union-find cycle test and with the rational
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1} of
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t}.
\item
  The parity-forced residual has a dual certificate. An even subgraph
  \texttt{z} has
  \texttt{<\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
  for every assignment \texttt{f}, so
  \texttt{<\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1}
  rules out every repair family at once. This is the
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}2} counterpart of the circulation
  dual of \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1}.
\item
  The source's ``Adm-indexed
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1}'' is a Hamming
  distance over \texttt{F\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}2} with unit
  weights. It is named
  \texttt{b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l}.
  It is not the rational quotient mass of
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l}.
\item
  The exchange dichotomy uses two separate hypotheses:
  \texttt{x\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1}
  must force
  \texttt{x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}1}
  (an integral domain), and
  \texttt{+\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}1}.
  \texttt{Z\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}8} has four characters and
  \texttt{Z\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2} has one. Over \texttt{Q} and
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})} both hypotheses
  hold.
\item
  P7-C10 is false as stated, under either reading. Read on the affine
  Bloch map,
  \texttt{g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1}
  fails for the replacement channel. Read on the linear part, a strict
  contraction is not necessary for loss: dephasing and
  measure-and-prepare lose coherence at norm exactly one. For qubits the
  linear part of a positive trace-preserving map always has norm at most
  one, because the Bloch ball maps into itself; the tests check this on
  the declared channels only. The row is now typed
  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N},
  citing the countermodel test.
\item
  The finite product-pattern obligation is discharged by exhaustive Rust
  computation over all 16 families on the edge, not by Lean.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} P7-C6 and P7-C7, the price list and its
completeness reading, stay open and interpretive. Their finite parts are
computed elsewhere: the phase fiber as the
mass\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}phase embedding of §11.1, the
interference boundary in QM\_061's entry, and the Mermin--Peres parity
core in
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e}.
Continuity of dynamics has no finite content. P7-C8's claim about
derivability, and P7-C9's naming ruling, have no finite content beyond
the rows above. No qubit, Hilbert space or Bloch sphere is derived; the
qubit Bloch maps are declared channels.

\subsubsection{11.33 Correlation, separability, and finite Bell
bounds}\label{correlation-separability-and-finite-bell-bounds}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Correlation, separability,
and finite Bell bounds
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper proved three finite results. Every bare joint table is a
mixture of point product tables. Every box with a single joint table
satisfies
\texttt{|\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2}.
Exchange equivariance under the alternating character removes weight
from diagonal loci. It then priced the ways past the bound. All three
results now compute exactly, together with the two boxes that go past
the bound without a joint table: the PR box, and an entangled box with
rational entries. Its annex, QM\_074, is covered here.

  states

\textbf{What stays outside.} P8-C10: applying Bell's theorem to nature
requires local-response factorization, setting independence and an
empirical identification of preparations, settings and outcomes. No
continuum premise is needed for the finite CHSH contradiction. P8-C11:
the physics readings. The Tsirelson ceiling {[}17{]} and attaining
witness are now derived \textbf{inside a supplied finite quantum model};
tensor composition, positivity, the state, observables and
trace\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}Born pairing remain declarations rather
than consequences of \texttt{<\allowbreak{}>}.

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} CPTP trace-norm geometry
and quantum dual witnesses
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper puts the trace distance \(\frac12\|\cdot\|_1\) on Hermitian
trace-zero edge defects of a finite directed graph, takes the quotient
by trace-zero vertex repairs, and describes its dual by bounded
divergence-free observable circulations.
\texttt{t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}
now certifies that quotient exactly. A primal certificate (repairs and
PSD splits of the residuals) bounds it from above, a dual certificate
(edge observables in operator-norm balls, decided by exact PSD tests)
bounds it from below, and the value is returned only when the two agree.
\texttt{t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e}
supplies the exact trace norms, the operator-norm balls, the dual-ball
lemma and the qubit closed form, and
\texttt{d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l}
