\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{The dual formula.} Theorem 5 states
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \Phi=\max_M\sum_e\operatorname{Tr}(M_e\delta_e)\)}\]
  over \(d_0^*M=0\) with
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \lambda_{\max}(M_e)-\lambda_{\min}(M_e)\leq1\)}\].
  That statement is right, and it is what the lower bound checks (one
  centre \texttt{c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e} per edge). But the
  proof ends, and Theorem 6's set \texttt{W}, the §2.6b dual SDP, §2.8's
  \texttt{W\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r} and §2.9
  continue, with centred witnesses (\(\|M_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq1/2\))
  that are exactly divergence-free. That set is the dual of the quotient
  by \emph{all} Hermitian repairs, scalar parts included. The proof's
  step ``finite iff
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}''
  is, for trace-zero repairs, ``finite iff every
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}*\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}v}
  is a multiple of \texttt{I}'', and §2.6b drops the multipliers of its
  own trace-zero constraints. On
  \texttt{K\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\}}
  with defects
  \texttt{3\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}I}
  the trace-zero quotient is \texttt{6}; every exactly divergence-free
  witness of operator norm at most
  \texttt{1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2}, centred or not, gives at most
  \texttt{9\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2}, which the all-Hermitian repair
  certifies. Centring the right witness is harmless for the value but
  moves the divergence to a multiple of \texttt{I}. The two quotients
  agree on qubits (scalar parts never lower the trace norm of a
  trace-zero
  \texttt{2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2}
  matrix) and on a single cycle, for every \texttt{n}, so the gap needs
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3}
  and two independent cycles. Those two agreements are prose arguments;
  the tests check one qubit packet and three cycles. The source's tests
  covered only cycles, trees and qubits, and its LP code centred the
  multipliers and noted that the divergence was then zero ``modulo
  scalar identity''.
\item
  \textbf{Selection.} Under axiom 1 (absolute homogeneity) and axiom 2
  (CPTP monotonicity) the gauge is already \(c\|\cdot\|_1\). The
  measure-and-prepare map of
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l}
  sends any trace-zero \texttt{X} to any \texttt{Y} with
  \(\|Y\|_1\leq\|X\|_1\), so a CPTP-monotone gauge is a nondecreasing
  function of the trace norm, and the embedding pair gives one
  \texttt{c} for all dimensions. CPTP monotonicity is therefore not
  inert: it implies unitary invariance and fixes total-variation
  reduction up to that scale. What it leaves free is one number.
  PL-005-2 (a CPTP-monotone norm not proportional to the trace norm) is
  answered in the negative for every norm, not only in the Schatten
  family. Inside one dimension the countermodels need
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3}
  (Hilbert--Schmidt) and
  \texttt{n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}4}
  (operator norm); on trace-zero qubits every unitarily invariant norm
  is a multiple of the trace norm.
\item
  \textbf{Exactness.} The source solved the duality numerically (HiGHS,
  ADMM) with tolerances. Here nothing is optimised over matrices:
  certificates are declared or built in closed form and replayed
  exactly. For diagonal defects the value comes from
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s}
  on a stacked cochain with a declared rational repair map
  (\texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s}
  proposes,
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l}
  replays), and the replayed witnesses are lifted to matrix certificates
  that the packet verifier checks independently. Trace norms come from
  sign certificates when the spectrum is rational and from the closed
  surd form on qubits; both results are now exact.
\item
  \textbf{Lean.} The package's
  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}Z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n}
  and its axiom-printing companion
  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}Z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n}
  now live in
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}.
  They are Mathlib-free. Their report was produced on
  \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}0};
  a staging build on the workspace toolchain
  \texttt{v\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}1}
  compiled them with the same axioms
  (\texttt{p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t}
  and
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d}
  at most; the coboundary lemmas use none). That is a build, not a

  verifies the dual-ball identity for two-point integer spectra
  (\texttt{E\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}2}), the scaling

  \texttt{h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t}
  over \texttt{R\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}n} in

\textbf{What stays outside.} The corrected duality is computed on
declared packets only. Nothing here solves the matrix SDP: for defects
with irrational spectra on graphs with several cycles, a value is
certified only when certificates are declared. C1 and C4 stay
conditional on the operational axioms; C5 (necessity), C7 (the wider
monotone landscape) and the definitions C3, C8 and C13 are unchanged,
although C13's remark that any maximizer over
\texttt{W\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r} attains
\texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r}
fails on the same countermodel. Reading
\texttt{M\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e} as a measurable observable,
binary discrimination as an experiment, and every physical reading of
the graph stay outside.

\subsubsection{11.36 Trace-norm transport under quantum
channels}\label{trace-norm-transport-under-quantum-channels}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Trace-norm CPTP transport
audit
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The audit separated three statements under declared imports: CPTP
monotonicity does not select the trace distance; the trace norm
contracts under CPTP maps (imported as the data-processing inequality);
and the classical shadow of that contraction, \texttt{l\allowbreak{}1}
contraction under stochastic kernels. All three now compute exactly, and
the first is sharper than stated. The measure-and-prepare maps of
\texttt{d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l}
show that CPTP monotonicity leaves exactly one free scale for a norm of
differences, not a family of rival norms.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{The firewall is pinned down.} A functional of trace-zero
  differences that never increases under CPTP maps \(M_n\to M_n\) is a
  nondecreasing function of the trace norm: for \(\|Y\|_1\leq\|X\|_1\)
  the map
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle Z\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(PZ)A+\operatorname{Tr}((I-P)Z)B\)}\],
  with \(P\) the projector onto the nonnegative part of \texttt{X} and
  \texttt{A}, \texttt{B} states built from the Jordan parts of \(Y\), is
  CPTP and sends \(X\) to \(Y\). For norms this leaves \(c\|\cdot\|_1\)
  only, so CPTP monotonicity plus absolute homogeneity selects the trace
  distance up to one normalization. The breadth that C6 and QM-091-N2
  cite (relative entropies, fidelity quantities, monotone metrics)
  belongs to functionals of the \emph{pair}
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{})},
  not of the difference. QM-091-N2's ``infinitely many
  unitarily-invariant norms \ldots{} are CPTP-monotone'' is false beyond
  rescaling: the Schatten norms with
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1}
  grow under \texttt{T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}B}
  (QM\_080), the Hilbert--Schmidt norm grows
  \texttt{3\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2}
  (squared) between two qutrit differences of trace norm \texttt{2}, and
  the operator norm grows
  \texttt{1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1}
  between two four-level ones, each time through an exact CPTP map.
\item
  \textbf{Falsifiability condition (i) is not met.} The structural
  imports with CPTP monotonicity fix the functional only up to a
  nondecreasing reparametrization of the trace norm (up to scale for
  norms). The normalization still comes from the imported discrimination
  axiom.
\item
  \textbf{Non-vacuity.} The Lean seal used the halving step
  \texttt{x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2}
  over \texttt{N}, which is not a channel. The witness is now a genuine
  CPTP strict contraction, decided on a basis of the trace-zero space.
\item
  \textbf{Contraction.} The paper imported data processing. The
  Heisenberg certificate verifies it on each declared channel and input:
  \texttt{L\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}*}
  is unital and positive, so it keeps the operator unit ball, and it
  moves the optimal witness back to the input.
\item
  \textbf{Lean.}
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t},

  and
  \texttt{0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n}
  (ENC-0247, ENC-0246, ENC-1055) are not in the repository. The Rust

\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The four imports (QM-091-D1) and the
non-claims (QM-091-N1) stay fences. The Helstrom reading as an
operational experiment (C3) and data processing as a general theorem
(C4) stay imported; the computations above are instances. QM-091-N2 is
not retyped: its breadth clause is false for norms, as shown. The
classification of monotone metrics on pairs (Petz, Morozova--Chentsov)
is not computed.

The paper's one theorem is elementary: stochastic kernels carry
distributions to distributions and compose, and a CPTP map read on the
output diagonal of a declared basis induces a stochastic population

diagonality, does not determine the channel, and does not force complete
positivity. Each is now an exact computation. The shadow is
\texttt{p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w},

and channels come from
\texttt{e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l}.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The kernel is stored row stochastic,
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}]\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}]\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}K\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{})},
  the transpose of the paper's column convention, as in
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w}
  and
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s}.
\item
  Composition. Kernels compose, as (ii) says, but the population shadow
  of a composite channel is not the composite of the shadows. The
  descent from channels to kernels respects composition when the first
  map leaves only populations, and not in general.
\item
  The lift. Every stochastic kernel does have a completely positive
  lift, the measure-and-prepare map with a diagonal Choi matrix, so
  ``the lift is not implied'' means that it is not unique (identity and
  dephasing share a kernel) and that a positive map with a stochastic
  kernel need not be completely positive (the transpose). It does not
  mean that a kernel may lack a CPTP pre-image.
\item
  The cited Lean module
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l}
  (ENC-1127:
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x},
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e},
  \texttt{k\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c})
  is not in the repository, so the row's ``MECHANIZED'' status had no
  surviving evidence. C4 is now a finite computation on declared kernels
  and channels; the general statement is the paper's prose proof.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The carrier and kernel definitions
(C1--C3), the green\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}red firewall and authority
fence (C9, C10) and the literature comparison (C11) are unchanged. C9's
clause that CPTP monotonicity does not select the trace-norm gauge is
sharpened in QM\_081: it leaves one free scale. When coherence transport
is admissible (the ``harder rung'' of the support ledger) is not
addressed. C5, C7 and C8 keep their types; the report suggests retypes.

boundary
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

\textbf{Corrections and scope.} C3 claimed that local positivity
\texttt{K\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
does not force complete positivity
\texttt{K\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}.
On the classical carrier the stub names, it does: a nonnegative kernel
tensored with an identity is still nonnegative, and its
measure-and-prepare lift is completely positive. The gap between
positivity and complete positivity opens only for maps that move
coherence, such as the transpose. The cited Lean targets
(\texttt{0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n},
\texttt{0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n},
\texttt{0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n},
\texttt{0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n})
do not exist in
\texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/};
C3 cited a non-selection file for a positivity claim.

\textbf{What stays outside.} C4's reading of a Kraus decomposition as an
``external \texttt{L\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2}
observer projection'' is interpretive; its finite content is that the
decomposition is not determined by the channel. No continuum statement
is made.

\subsubsection{11.39 Operational equivalence and interpretive
underdetermination}\label{operational-equivalence-and-interpretive-underdetermination}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Interpretations and
operational equivalence
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper reads the interpretations of quantum mechanics as narratives
laid over one finite packet calculus, and gives one sharp criterion: a
reading becomes adjudicable only when it changes a packet number. It
formalizes no new theorem of its own. Its residual signature, its
distinguishability criterion, its worked example and its two
non-implications have finite content, and all of them now compute. The
six interpretation rows are prose and get no code.

  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1},
  and
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l}
  refuses the same certificate reporting
  \texttt{9\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0}.
\item
  ``Classical gluing failure does not imply complex Hilbert QM'' is
  witnessed twice: in the paper's own formalism by a graph cycle, and in
  the Kochen--Specker sense by real rays. The same countermodels decide
  C3, which the source typed
  \texttt{O\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N}. The
  reconstruction question it points to is C4, and that stays open.
\item
  The firewall ENC-1063 was cited as a Lean theorem. No such file is in
  the tree. Its Rust form is
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}'
  sealed authority constructor, which this crate cannot name; the row
  now cites
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}'
  own tests and the worked instance of QM\_091.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The interpretation classifier (C6, C8) is
narrative. The reconstruction conjecture and its five-condition target
(C2, C4, C5) stay \texttt{O\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N}.
The registry-relative lift (C11, C12) belongs to QM\_001. No
interpretation is scored true or false, and nothing here grants
authority.

\subsubsection{11.40 Formal possibility is not physical
realization}\label{formal-possibility-is-not-physical-realization}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Deutsch, Everett, Wolfram,
and the promotion error
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper states one typed non-implication, that deriving a structure
does not mint authority, and applies it as three argued readings of
Deutsch, Everett--DeWitt and Wolfram. Its finite content is small: the
worked instance of the type separation, and the firewall itself, whose
Rust form is the sealed authority constructor in
\texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}.
The three readings, the fairness ledger and the appendix on Deutsch's
resource count are prose.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The ledger row stated the instance as
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})}:
  two weights for one edge. That is refused as malformed. With one
  weight it is a single edge, on which every residual is a repair
  (\texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}).
  The body's version,
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2},
  is the one implemented, over \texttt{Q}.
\item
  The body computed \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1}
  ``by the declared finite rule'' without giving the value. It is
  \texttt{1}, proposed by
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s}
  and replayed by
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l}.
\item
  ``The structure fixes the diagnostic, the packet fixes the authority''
  is now precise. Of the ten fields of
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}'
  guard evidence, the structure supplies one, the residual mass; the
  others are declarations it does not contain. A test that filled the
  guard evidence from the structure was dropped at integration, because
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s}
  must not name
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}
  (\texttt{c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e});
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}'
  own tests cover the guard logic.
\item
  Tier 1b (authority factors only through
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}p})
  is superseded in the source itself and stays
  \texttt{O\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N}.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The Deutsch, Everett--DeWitt and Wolfram
readings (C5, C6, C8, C10, C12, C13), their defeat conditions (C16), the
conditional physical no-go (C7) and the finiteness argument against the
resource-count reading of Deutsch (Appendix A) are argued prose with no
finite object. The mathematical core of the Everett reading, that a
branch representation is not fixed by the state, is computed under
QM\_092 (C23) and QM\_094.

decidable classifier or a typed non-implication, and imports thirteen

there. This entry computes the kernels the suite owns, exhaustively on
declared boxes of cochains, and points the rest at their owners.

  restate \texttt{C\allowbreak{}1}..\texttt{C\allowbreak{}9} and are

\subsubsection{11.43 Everettian relative
states}\label{everettian-relative-states}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Everettian relative-state
contact
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper gives the relative-state formalism a finite anatomy: squared
coefficients form an \texttt{L\allowbreak{}1} shadow, record overlaps
and phases carry the \texttt{L\allowbreak{}2} coherence, and U(1)
holonomy matters only where histories recombine. Every positive
statement is conditional on a declared Hilbert carrier and
factorization, and all of them now compute exactly over
\texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})}. The ontology,
preferred-basis and probability rows stay open or refused, and the
refusals now rest on exact countermodels.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Coefficients are declared up to a positive scale, so equal-weight
  branches such as
  \texttt{1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2}
  need no surd. Records must be exact unit vectors.
\item
  Witness 3.2's
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2}
  is evaluated at unit Gaussian rationals \texttt{u} as
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2}.
  That covers the requested
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
  and
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i},
  and three intermediate phases, exactly.
\item
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f}
  is a sum of moduli, which are generally irrational over
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})}. It is returned
  only when every summand is rational and refused otherwise. The
  hypothesis \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq1\) is decided exactly as
  \(I-A^*A\succeq0\).
\item
  The multiplicity warning is computed: the refinement that conserves
  squared-norm weight changes the share of branch labels.
\item
  The tree and diamond statements are computed by QM\_063's module,
  which is the ``Quantum Contact 1'' this paper cites, rather than by a
  second copy.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} Many-worlds ontology (C11) and a preferred
basis from holonomy (C9) stay refused. The countermodel shows that the
branch decomposition is not a function of the state; that is the reason
for the refusal, not a proof that the Everett reading is wrong.
Everettian probability (C12) stays open: the weights are a normalized
valuation conserved under refinement, and branch counting is another
normalized valuation that is not, so normalization alone does not choose
between them. No dynamics, decoherence rate or collapse model is
implemented.

(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper reads a fault-tolerance threshold theorem as a conditional
repair-capacity certificate: under the theorem's own hypotheses it fills
the repair-capacity packet, and below threshold the
projection-obstruction no-go does not fire. The threshold theorems are
imported, not re-proved. What follows from their declared numbers now
computes in
\texttt{t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e},

\texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y},

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  Theorem 1 is right and tight, but its proof compared \texttt{e} with
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c}.
  The argument that works is about the decoder: two errors of weight at
  most \texttt{t} with one syndrome differ by a cocycle of weight at
  most
  \texttt{2\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d},
  hence by a coboundary. Tightness is the split of a minimal logical
  operator.
\item
  A cochain code covers one Pauli type. The three-qubit bit-flip code
  has bit-flip distance 3 and code distance 1, since a single \texttt{Z}
  is logical. The claim that fault-tolerant syndromes ``are'' coboundary
  defects holds for CSS codes read off a complex, one error type at a
  time; the five-qubit code is not CSS, and its distance comes from the
  stabilizer module.
\item
  The second half of C3 is false as stated. For maximum-likelihood
  decoding the failure probability is at most
  \texttt{1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}|}
  on every code and at every noise level: for each syndrome it keeps the
  largest of
  \texttt{|\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}|}
  class probabilities, which is at least their mean. Failure approaching
  1 is a property of a fixed decoder, here minimum weight, not of the
  code. The asymptotic statement itself is not computed.
\item
  \texttt{d} is undefined when
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0};
  such a code is refused
  (\texttt{N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}Q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t}).
\item
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}Q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e}
  declared
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3}
  and
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s}
  declared
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2}
  for
  \texttt{[\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}]\allowbreak{}]};
  both now compute \texttt{n}, \texttt{k} and \texttt{d} from the
  generators (§5, stabilizer code distance), and the computed distances
  agree with the former declarations.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} No threshold value is computed, and nothing
is said about code families as they grow beyond the declared instances.
C4, the quarantine of continuum qudit baths, is a scope fence. The Lean
targets the ledger names
(\texttt{0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n},
\texttt{0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n})
are not in the repository, and the shared-kernel theorem of its
mechanization line is the integer fact QM\_101 records.

\subsubsection{11.47 An evidence-presentation
protocol}\label{an-evidence-presentation-protocol}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Show-the-packet protocol
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper is a protocol, not a theorem: a claim of scalable physical
quantum computation must expose a finite packet of declared fields
before the checker reports a result, and each missing or invalid field
has a stated rejection reason. Its support record asks for the decision
procedure itself.
\texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}e}
is that procedure: it refuses in the protocol's order, replays the
finite algebra the packet declares, and computes the terminal instead of
accepting one.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The vocabulary had no refusal for two fields the packet requires, the
  closure map \texttt{d\allowbreak{}1} and the mixing bound
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}.
  \texttt{N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p}
  and
  \texttt{N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d}
  are added.
  \texttt{q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i}
  and
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s}
  are computed by the checker, not declared.
\item
  The paper names outputs and works one example; it states no decision
  rule. The recurrence is a lower bound. It can establish failure when
  the bound crosses the visibility threshold, but failure of the bound
  to cross establishes no survival statement. For example, with initial
  residual \(1\), gap \(0\), and threshold \(2\), both \(r_n=1\) and
  \(r_n=1+n\) satisfy \(r_{n+1}\ge r_n+0\); one remains below the
  threshold and the other crosses it. The checker therefore reports
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d},
  not success, whenever this lower bound is inconclusive. A positive
  finite-window conclusion would require an upper bound, an exact
  trajectory check, or another sufficient argument. A claim at
  human-significant scale can only get the conditional result of an
  imported threshold scaling with
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h},
  with a theorem among the declared evidence and a nonpositive gap. A
  missing claim scope is
  \texttt{N\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e};
  a finite packet offered for an asymptotic claim is
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h},
  the escalation described in §9 of the source paper.
\item
  Evidence is declared as a set of sources (theorem, experiment,
  simulation), so a combination says which sources it combines.
\item
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1} of the defect
  history is certified by
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y}
  with unit weights; no declared value of it is trusted.
\item
  This paper's claim IDs repeat QM\_101's
  (\texttt{Q\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}1}
  to
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}4});
  only the \texttt{1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}:} prefix
  in the ledger separates them.
\item
  The ENC entries the ledger cites as mechanized (ENC-1063, 1065, 1066,
  1067,

  \begin{enumerate}
  \def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi})}
  \setcounter{enumi}{1070}
  \tightlist
  \item
    have no Lean source in the repository.
  \end{enumerate}
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The fences and doctrine (C2, C8, C9, C13,
C14), the open questions at human-significant scale (C10), the notation
row (C12) and the positioning of threshold theorems (C6). The finite
checks do show one half of C13: the fields that are replayed cannot be
satisfied by an arbitrary value. A complete packet yields a terminal
status, never authority.

\subsubsection{11.48 Loop quantum gravity kinematical
models}\label{loop-quantum-gravity-kinematical-models}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Loop quantum gravity
kinematical models
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper collects finite shadows of five kinematical motifs of loop
quantum gravity, each on a toy carrier, and cites seven Lean files for
them. None of those files is in the repository; their text survives as
reading guides in
\texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/}.
The shadows now compute: connections and loop holonomy through
\texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y},
the quaternion group and the flux operators in
\texttt{q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w},
the spin-\texttt{j} Casimir and the area labels in
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m}.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  All seven Lean modules are cited as mechanized, and none is present.

  is in
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n}
  as the integer fact
  \texttt{a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
  for
  \texttt{a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b};
  no holonomy appears in it. The rows now rest on exact Rust checks:
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N}
  where a general statement is checked on declared instances,
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}A}
  where a finite statement is decided completely.
\item
  The Casimir value
  \texttt{j\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})},
  imported in the source, is computed on the spin-\texttt{j}
  representation of
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})} in
  a rational basis. That the flux acts as \texttt{J} at a puncture, the
  area operator and the scale
  \texttt{8\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2}
  stay imported.
\item
  \texttt{q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}p}
  builds \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}8} through
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}x}
  (\texttt{a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}Z\allowbreak{})}),

\textbf{What stays outside.} Continuum
\texttt{S\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})} with

\subsubsection{11.49 General relativity kinematical
models}\label{general-relativity-kinematical-models}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} General relativity
kinematical models
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The GR sibling of QM\_110: curvature as non-abelian holonomy, a
Bianchi-shaped identity, metric compatibility, parallel transport, the
singularity as a refusal and the continuum as a certified limit, each on
a toy carrier with a Lean file that is not in the repository. The first

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The finite Bianchi shadow
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
  is abelian and holds on every complex. Its non-abelian form needs base
  points: the discrete identity holds for face loops transported to one
  vertex and fails, with value \texttt{-\allowbreak{}1}, for face loops
  based at their own first vertices.
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y}'s
  \texttt{v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y}
  checks the based form; its documentation states the identity without
  that condition.
\item
  ``Which pairing is the metric is imported'' is exhibited: the same
  transport is an isometry of one declared pairing and not of another.
\item
  The singularity row became an orbit dichotomy. On a finite carrier,
  incompleteness is decided within as many steps as there are vertices.
\item
  The six Lean modules the paper cites are not in the repository; the
  reading guides keep them. Its shared-kernel citation,
  \texttt{h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n},
  is integer subtraction (see QM\_110).
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The continuum limit (C5b) is a
\texttt{T\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o}
statement and stays
\texttt{A\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D};
a continuum object without a convergence certificate is held by the
membrane of
\texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}q}.
The manifold, the metric, the Levi-Civita connection, the Riemann and
Einstein tensors and the gauge group (C1b, C7), the Einstein equation
(C8), the readings (C6) and the non-claims (C9).

\subsubsection{11.50 Mermin--Peres contextuality as a parity
obstruction}\label{merminperes-contextuality-as-a-parity-obstruction}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Mermin--Peres
contextuality and cochain obstruction
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper packaged the Mermin--Peres square as a finite parity packet:
nine variables, six row and column contexts, sign
\texttt{-\allowbreak{}1} on the third column and
\texttt{+\allowbreak{}1} elsewhere, and the statement that this sign
vector lies outside the image of the incidence coboundary over
\texttt{F\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}2}. Its Lean modules survive only
as uncompiled Markdown transcriptions under
\texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/},
and its certificate generator is not in the package.
\texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t}
now decides the packet exactly, with certificates, a complete census of
the \texttt{5\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2} assignments and a second
decision through the Cech complex of
\texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}.
\texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e}
computes the sign table from Mermin's two-qubit Pauli operators, which
the paper had left as a future target.

Five rungs were already computed by library modules; the missing one,

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The worked example's lift
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})}
  is irrational. Over
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})} the point
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{})}
  has no preimage at all
  (\texttt{3\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}6} is not a sum of
  two rational squares), so the redundancy of the Born square is shown
  on
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{})},
  where exact lifts exist.
\item
  The shadow is stored row stochastic, rows indexed by inputs, so that
  it is applied by the existing
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d};
  the ladder's column-stochastic
  \texttt{K\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})}
  is its transpose.
\item
  ``Channels compose'' holds for kernels, not for shadows. The shadow of
  a rotation followed by itself is
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{};\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}5},
  while the product of the two shadows is
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{};\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}5}.
  The defect vanishes when the first channel keeps diagonal inputs
  diagonal or the second reads only populations (dephasing, bit flip,
  amplitude damping), and not otherwise: the coherence the first step
  creates is interference for the second.
\item
  Rung 5's fiber is enumerated only for declared finite unit groups.
  QM\_122 shows that the mixing leftover already runs on
  \texttt{\{\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\}},
  so the circle \texttt{U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})} of
  the source's
  \texttt{U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})}
  is not constructed here.
\item
  The four Lean rows
  (\texttt{P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}Q\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y},
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y},
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l},
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}S\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m})
  are not in the repository. The rows now rest on the Rust above, not on
  a Lean replay.
\item
  C7's ``proven predicate equivalence'' is a definition apart from the
  race condition, as QM\_061 recorded.
\end{itemize}
