\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  C12 said the square agrees with itself only on the two exhibited
  frames and that global frame additivity was not proved. At scale 2 it
  is now decided: the square's frame total is
  \texttt{<\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}>},
  and each of the 96 orthogonal scale-2 frames has
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}I},
  so the constraint holds for every state of
  \texttt{Z\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}]\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2}.
  Powers 2--4 violate it. At scale 1 the frames are the coordinate axes
  up to units and no power is excluded, so the constraint discriminates
  from scale 2 on.
\item
  C43 is false as stated, and its row is now
  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N};
  the ray, pair, tetrad and parity counts it also states hold and are
  computed above. All 146 vertices of the Cabello frame polytope are
  non-Bornian (not PSD), but none has least eigenvalue below
  \texttt{-\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2}: exactly 26 reach
  \texttt{-\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2} and the other 120
  stay above \texttt{-\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}4}. The
  source's claim
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}5}
  holds for no vertex. The enumeration covers every basis of the
  incidence (each ray lies in exactly two tetrads, so bases are
  unicyclic subgraphs of the tetrad graph, solved by peeling and checked
  against
  \texttt{A\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1}).
\item
  C49 is false in three places
  (\texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N}).
  The two matrices the source calls canonical extreme vertices are
  feasible frame functions with 12 nonzero coordinates, more than
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}9},
  so they are not vertices. The 18 ray projectors are states but are not
  vertices either (support 11). ``Eliminating vertices with
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2}''
  describes 26 of 146 vertices. In the source code the ``glued 2-simplex
  interface operator'' is the identity matrix and its boundary condition
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
  follows from positivity, so the filter is the PSD test; it removes
  every vertex.
\item
  C51 is false as stated
  (\texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N}).
  The closure condition
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}\{\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}\}}
  does not confine \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u} to the listed
  spectrum in
  \texttt{Z\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}]}:
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1}
  gives the eighth turn, with
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}I}
  and
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}I},
  so its eigenvalue has order 8 and does not lie in
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})};
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u} is a root of none of the listed
  polynomials. The source's per-hinge list gives
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1}
  for order 12 and misses
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2},
  which has order exactly 12 and solves
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}.
  The listed
  \texttt{1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3}
  squares to \texttt{1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}3} and is not an

  The ``retarded'' parameter
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})}
  is the Cayley parameter of the turn by
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0}
  followed by the inverse turn by
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s}; it is below
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0}
  only when
  \texttt{1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
  (\texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}2},
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1}

\item
  C46:
  \texttt{I\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}
  alone does not select
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2};
  the linear readout also has it. Only together with

  is \texttt{p\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2}
  singled out among the powers.
\item
  C40's ``discrete Gleason scaling uniqueness'' is the
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}2} scaling of the unnormalized Hadamard on
  declared vectors, not a Gleason-type theorem.
\item
  C48: no 6j symbol or Biedenharn--Elliott identity is computed
  anywhere; the check the source names a pentagon is the braid relation

\item
  C52--C65 put physical names on declared arithmetic. The bound
  \texttt{S\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}4}
  is the declared unit
  \texttt{A\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d};
  no Schmidt decomposition is computed. The Page curve's zero endpoint
  is the declared schedule. Total Bianchi force and torque vanish for
  arbitrary declared weights (they are sums of opposite pairs), while
  vertex sums do not;
  \texttt{J\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}J\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}R}
  is conserved by construction for arbitrary
  \texttt{(\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{})};
  the four-simplex sum vanishes for arbitrary hinge weights, which is
  \texttt{∂\allowbreak{}∂\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}.
  The constraint ``bracket'' is a commutator of two rational numbers,
  always 0, so the ``anomaly'' is minus the induced term. The spin-foam
  amplitudes are signs, so orientation ``conjugation'' holds because
  they are real. On the eight admissible four-spin boundaries every
  transition is 1: the vacuum column has squared norm 8, so C61's
  unitarity fails for the paper's model
  (\texttt{M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d});
  the row is now
  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N}.
  The Pachner ``partition'' multiplies an amplitude by itself: amplitude
  \texttt{i} gives \texttt{-\allowbreak{}1}. C64 does not claim a norm,
  so it keeps its type, with this defect recorded here.
\item
  The copies in
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}

  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}7} have since been

  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m}

  \texttt{M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}
  is the paper's model, the one the ledger rows C57 to C64 describe, so

  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N};
  its evidence now also cites the corrected model's test, marked as a

  \texttt{M\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}

  \texttt{a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}I}

  \texttt{a\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0},
  and the partition as a Hermitian norm on every declared amplitude
  (table above). Nothing here claims unitarity of a general spin foam.
\item
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}9} corrects the
  Cayley numerator of a zero generator, a closed form that the Rust

  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m}
  solves the transform exactly and agrees with the corrected numerator,

\item
  \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n}
  reported seven ``checks'' that were constant expressions

  \texttt{1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2},
  \texttt{2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3},
  \texttt{4\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}4},
  \texttt{i\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1},
  \texttt{I\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}!\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0},
  \texttt{|\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1})
  and were not tied to the claims they were named after; each now

  not rely on them.
\item
  The E8 enumeration in
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}
  takes about a minute in a debug build; it is cited through its own

\item
  C12 is now
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}A}:
  every statement in the row holds, and its remark that global frame
  additivity is not proved is superseded at scale 2. C9, C13 and C39
  were fixtures and are now
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N},
  as are C14, C22, C23, C40, C41, C42 and C47; C45 and C46 are
  \texttt{E\allowbreak{}X\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}L\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}A}.
\item
  The Lean did not move. The package's 52 Lean modules are also tracked,
  byte for byte, in
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/},
  whose axiom report and build receipt the
  \texttt{L\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{})}
  rows cite, so the rows still resolve after the paper is deleted.
  Against
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}:
  8 modules are identical, 29 differ only in how they spell their
  imports, 9 have diverged (the corrected
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}9},
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}5} and
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}7} among them), and
  6 have no counterpart
  (\texttt{H\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0},
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2} and four
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}*} threads, which import files
  that exist only in
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s}).
  Moving them would change what the receipts describe, so they stay with
  their receipts.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} The receipted Lean rows keep their type;
Rust replays are not substitutes. C0, C19 and C20 are fences, C15
describes the Lean assembly, C16 points at §7. C38 (the Python dual) is
untyped; its finite content is computed by
\texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r}
and the tests above. C44's MIP and Lie algebra parts, C50's ``layer
admission residue'', C55's Lean and every physical reading of C52--C65
are not modelled. Ordinary
\texttt{M\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{})},
Gleason uniqueness at
\texttt{n\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3},
CPTP channels, Hilbert-tensor uniqueness, the circle group and
continuous time remain imports, as the paper says.

\subsubsection{11.54 Boundary synthesis and cochain
lifts}\label{boundary-synthesis-and-cochain-lifts}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Universal boundary
synthesis and cochain lift
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper claims that every earlier contact point factors through one
exact sequence
\texttt{0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0},
that a descent functor to finite Hilbert spaces is neither full nor
faithful, and that the pointer basis is the zero-curvature kernel
\texttt{k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}1}.
The asserted initial exactness fails on every nonempty graph complex
with ordinary vertex cochains, because constants are killed by
\texttt{d\allowbreak{}0}. The pointer basis is not determined by the
complex: the counterexample below changes it while keeping the complex
fixed. The proposed functor is not defined. What holds is computed here
or by the papers the synthesis cites.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  C1 is false as written, and its row is now
  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N}.
  Exactness at \texttt{C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}0}
  needs \texttt{d\allowbreak{}0} injective, and \texttt{d\allowbreak{}0}
  kills constants on every nonempty complex; exactness at
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1} needs
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}.
  With
  \texttt{O\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}1}
  the sequence is exact at its last two terms by definition, and
  \texttt{O\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}s} is
  \texttt{H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2} of the
  declared complex: zero for a disk, one-dimensional for a sphere. It is
  a topological invariant of the carrier, not a residual gap between
  cochain transport and quantum mechanics. The first term was declared
  as nonnegative \texttt{L\allowbreak{}1} weights, a cone rather than a
  group, and the U(1) transports of the second term form a
  multiplicative group, so no exact sequence of groups could start there
  in any case.
\item
  C4 is false
  (\texttt{R\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}D\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}Y\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N}).
  \texttt{k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}1}
  is fixed by the carrier, while the pointer basis is fixed by the
  declared environment; the dimensions differ as well. C7 stays
  \texttt{O\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N}: an undefined
  functor is not refuted by a computation.
\item
  C6 is true only on a declared 2-complex. On a carrier graph there are
  no 2-cochains (QM\_209).
\item
  C7: the functor sends
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{})}
  to endomorphisms of
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}V\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{})},
  which does not define a map on morphisms, so neither fullness nor
  faithfulness is a decidable statement. Its non-fullness bullet
  (continuous unitaries need a time parameter) is QM\_211's topic.
\item
  C3, ``contraction ratio invariance under cochain boundaries'', has no
  definition in the paper. The only reading that makes it a statement,
  composing a channel with gauge (diagonal unitary) channels, is unitary
  invariance of the trace norm, which belongs to QM\_080 and QM\_081;
  nothing was computed here.
\item
  The claimed ``replayable Python / Rust certifiers'' and the claim-code
  map point to a module that does not exist.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} C8, the scope limitation. The
category-theoretic framing is not modelled, no lift of weights is
constructed, and no physical statement follows from any of the
computations above.

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{11.55 Complex phase and \(U(1)\)
transport}{11.55 Complex phase and U(1) transport}}\label{complex-phase-and-u1-transport}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Complex phase fiber and
\(U(1)\) transport lift
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}7\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper's three mathematical statements are already computed by
QM\_060, QM\_062 and QM\_063's modules: weights are blind to vertex
phases, a phase-invariant cross term needs a conjugation, and the
relative transport of two paths is the holonomy of the loop they form.
This entry adds no code; it records which tests hold each statement and
what had to be corrected.

\subsubsection{\texorpdfstring{11.56 Quadratic \(L^2\) readout and the
cross-term interference
boundary}{11.56 Quadratic L\^{}2 readout and the cross-term interference boundary}}\label{quadratic-l2-readout-and-the-cross-term-interference-boundary}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Quadratic \(L^2\) readout
and interference boundary
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper separates the additive \(L^1\) readout from a quadratic
\(L^2\) readout and puts interference in the cross term
\[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle 2\operatorname{Re}(c_1\overline{c_2})\)}\].
The separation is right, but the displayed formula puts the cross term
in the wrong quantity: over orthonormal loci \(\|\psi\|^2\) has no cross
term. The cross term belongs to the recombined amplitude
\(|c_1+c_2|^2\), the quantity the abstract calls
\texttt{I\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}. Its
vanishing criterion also misses zero amplitudes. Both corrections
compute exactly over
\texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})}.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  §1's
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle P_{L^2}(\psi)=\|\psi\|^2=|c_1|^2+|c_2|^2+
  2\operatorname{Re}(c_1\overline{c_2})\)}\] is false for orthonormal
  \(|1\rangle,|2\rangle\). The right-hand side is
  \(|\langle\chi,\psi\rangle|^2\) for \(\chi=(1,1)\), the readout of the
  recombined amplitude. The norm itself is phase blind.
\item
  Theorem 2.1's criterion, nonzero ``iff
  \texttt{p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}2}
  is not
  \texttt{±\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i}'',
  needs
  \texttt{w\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0}:
  a zero amplitude carries every phase, including its partner's, and
  gives no cross term. Exactly: the cross term vanishes when
  \texttt{c\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}2}
  is imaginary, zero included.
\item
  C3's ``iff \texttt{l\allowbreak{}2} is imported'' is kept in its true
  half: the \texttt{L\allowbreak{}1} readout never shows a cross term.
  Importing the quadratic readout does not make it nonzero. The row
  stays \texttt{O\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}N}: read as
  ``a cross term can appear only once the quadratic readout is
  imported'' it holds, and read as a biconditional for every amplitude
  it fails as shown. C1 and C2 are
  \texttt{F\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}A\allowbreak{}T\allowbreak{}I\allowbreak{}O\allowbreak{}N}.
\item
  The claim-code map pointed to a module that does not exist; the audit
  row on ledger canonicality is refuted and is not cited.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} C4, the scope fence. Which readout is
imported is a declaration; nothing here selects the Born pairing or an
operator algebra.

\subsubsection{11.57 Noncommutative operator algebras and
contextuality}\label{noncommutative-operator-algebras-and-contextuality}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Noncommutative operator
algebra and contextuality
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper states that diagonal (\texttt{L\allowbreak{}1}) readouts
commute, that incompatible observables need non-diagonal matrices, and
that the Mermin--Peres parity contradiction is a nonzero class in
\texttt{H\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}G\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})}.
The first two compute directly. The third needs a correction: a carrier
graph has no 2-cochains, so the class exists only once a 2-complex whose
faces are the six contexts is declared. On such a complex it is computed
exactly over \texttt{F\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}2}.

pairing}\label{the-born-rule-and-stateeffect-pairing}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Born-rule postulate and
state-effect pairing
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

For positive real \(p\) and a nonzero vector, the paper's power rule
\(P_p(i)=|c_i|^p/\sum_j|c_j|^p\) is a probability vector in each
orthonormal context. Theorem 2.1 points to Gleason's theorem as one
route to selecting
\texttt{p\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2},
under noncontextuality, positivity and normalization on the full
projective domain in dimension at least three. The finite content
computes exactly on declared real rational contexts: each tested power
rule is a probability vector context by context; the square is basis
invariant by Parseval, whereas powers 1, 3 and 4 fail on the exhibited
three-dimensional contexts. In dimension two every positive-power rule
is context free, so the dimension hypothesis carries weight.
\texttt{p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s}
holds the rules and the search for a context dependence.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  ``\texttt{P\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p} defines a valid probability
  measure'' holds context by context only. For the nonzero vector
  \(\psi=(1,1,0)\), compare the standard basis with
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle (e_1,(3e_2+4e_3)/5,(-4e_2+3e_3)/5)\)}\].
  The common ray \(e_1\) has weight \(1/2\) in the first and
  \(1/(1+(3/5)^p+(4/5)^p)\) in the second. For \(p>0\), the sum
  \((3/5)^p+(4/5)^p\) is strictly decreasing and equals one precisely at
  \(p=2\). Thus every positive \(p\ne2\) fails context independence on
  this same rational pair of bases. This written argument covers all
  positive real powers; the exact native tests evaluate powers 1, 3 and
  4. At \(p=2\), Parseval gives the same total in every orthonormal
  context.
\item
  In dimension two a unit vector has one orthogonal complement up to
  sign, so every positive-power rule is context free there, and the
  first power is not of the form
  \texttt{<\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}>}
  for any Hermitian \texttt{r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o} (on real rays
  only the real part of \texttt{r\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o} acts).
  Non-contextuality does not select the square in dimension two; that is
  why Gleason's theorem needs dimension three.
\item
  Gleason is not needed to select the square within this power family.
  Its broader conclusion, that a nonnegative normalized frame assignment
  on the full real or complex Hilbert projective domain in dimension at
  least three is of Born form, is imported. The finite examples do not
  prove it on a restricted number field.
\item
  C2's ``non-linear'' holds in the amplitude only: the pairing is linear
  in the density matrix.
\item
  The paper's ``\texttt{L\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p} norm pairings''
  are powers of moduli, not norms. Complex amplitudes with irrational
  moduli are outside this exact carrier. The displayed integer-power
  checks use real rational vectors. The argument for arbitrary positive
  real powers uses ordinary real arithmetic; it is not claimed as a new
  exact native implementation or Lean proof.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} C4, the scope fence. Gleason's and Busch's
theorems and any physical selection of the pairing are not computed.

\subsubsection{11.59 Continuous unitary dynamics and the remaining
synthesis
problem}\label{continuous-unitary-dynamics-and-the-remaining-synthesis-problem}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} Continuous unitary
dynamics and \(L^1\)-to-quantum synthesis
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

Theorem 1.1 says that discrete stochastic steps cannot generate a
continuous unitary group without importing continuous time, a Hermitian
generator and a differentiable structure, and its proof says that
discrete steps allow only integer powers. The conclusion holds, for a
different reason. Stochastic steps can have fractional powers on
continuous stochastic semigroups; what they cannot be, short of a
permutation, is an \texttt{l\allowbreak{}2} isometry. So the stochastic
matrices meet the unitary group in a finite group, whatever time
parameter is declared.
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}
computes both halves. The five-import synthesis (C2, C3) is not a finite
statement.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  ``Discrete carrier steps permit only integer matrix powers'' is false:
  \texttt{[\allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}]\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}[\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}5\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{}]\allowbreak{}]}
  has a stochastic square root, and every two-state step with positive
  determinant lies on a semigroup
  \texttt{T\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{})} with a continuous
  parameter. The obstruction is isometry: an
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}2}-isometric stochastic matrix is a permutation
  matrix (a row with entries in
  \texttt{[\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}]}
  summing to one and squares summing to one has a single entry 1), so no
  nonconstant continuous path of unitaries runs through the stochastic
  matrices. The populations of a unitary step do not compose as a
  semigroup either (QM\_082,
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s}).
\item
  ``\texttt{U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{})} in
  \texttt{S\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}N\allowbreak{})}''
  is too narrow: a Hermitian generator gives a unitary, and with nonzero
  trace its Cayley step
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{})}
  has determinant \texttt{-\allowbreak{}i}.
\item
  No exponential is computed. The unitary family is the Cayley chart
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{})}
  of §11.19
  (\texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y}),
  and the stochastic semigroup is parametrised by
  \texttt{s\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}+\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{})}.
\item
  C3's ``five independent imports'' is not a finite statement:
  independence is not defined, and as written the Born import
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}>\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}2}
  already uses the inner product of the quadratic-readout import. The
  cascade's second step repeats QM\_208's misplaced cross term
  (\(\|\psi\|^2\) has none).
\item
  The cascade is not a minimal Bell price list. The exact static CHSH
  endpoint uses a bipartite composition, an entangled state,
  incompatible same-party observables and a positive
  trace\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}Born pairing. Its matrices are real
  and no continuous dynamics appears, so QM\_207's specifically complex
  phase fiber and QM\_211's continuous-time import are not individually
  necessary for Tsirelson saturation. Conversely, the five-item diagram
  omits the composition and locality structure that makes a Bell
  scenario a Bell scenario.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} C2 (the diagram), C3 (the synthesis
theorem) and C4 (space-time and ontology) have no finite content.
Continuous time, differentiability and Stone's theorem are not modelled.

\subsubsection{11.60 The Microsoft Majorana
problem}\label{the-microsoft-majorana-problem}

\textbf{Original paper in the paper archive:} The Microsoft Majorana
problem
(\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}d}).

The paper names a packet gap: hardware narratives about Majorana devices
and declared finite algebra live on different carriers, and neither
discharges the other. It keeps two exact cores, the
\texttt{G\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})}
residual trichotomy on declared complexes and specialized Ising
identities, and fences everything physical. The
\texttt{G\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})} core
already lives in the
\texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a}
crate and in QM\_120's
\texttt{p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t};
this entry does not duplicate it. What was missing is the declared
operator algebra that the Majorana and Ising vocabulary refers to. It
now computes exactly over
\texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})} in
\texttt{m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a}
and
\texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g}:
Jordan--Wigner Majoranas on a declared Fock space, the parity, a
declared Kitaev chain, Majorana braid unitaries whose restriction to a
parity sector is the paper's Ising pair, and the Ising fusion table.
None of it is evidence about a device.

\textbf{Corrections and scope.}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  The anticommutation check is
  \texttt{d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t}
  with a Euclidean metric (QM\_050);
  \texttt{f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e}
  only translates its refusals.
\item
  The paper points at
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a};
  the crate is
  \texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a}.
  Its
  \texttt{C\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}E\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t}
  multiplies in
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{})},
  but no braid identity is checked there. The braid relation is now
  checked over \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})}: the
  global phase
  \texttt{e\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}-\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}8\allowbreak{})}
  of the Ising \texttt{R} is the only part outside
  \texttt{Q\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{})}, and it cancels
  in every relation that is homogeneous in \texttt{R}.
\item
  The Ising matrices of §3.2 are the Majorana braid unitaries restricted
  to the even sector of two modes. The Kitaev sweet-spot statements are
  identities of declared matrices. The phase table
  \texttt{|\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}|\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}<\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}t}
  is not: at
  \texttt{m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2},
  inside it, the end Majorana is not conserved at any size checked, and
  on two modes the parity degeneracy splits.
\item
  ``Ising alone is computationally non-dense'' has a finite core: the
  braid image on the
  four-\texttt{s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a}
  space is a finite group of order 96, 24 up to scalars, so it is not
  dense in
  \texttt{S\allowbreak{}U\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})}.
  Computational density with supplements is not computed.
\item
  C13, the retraction of the old tetron carrier, is confirmed on the
  carrier rebuilt from its Python source.
\item
  C16's timing (17 ms per residual at
  \texttt{6\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}6}) is
  a measurement and is not reproduced. C17 stands: on
  \texttt{\{\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{},\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\}}
  vectors every powered norm is the weight, so every
  \texttt{l\allowbreak{}\textasciicircum{}\allowbreak{}p} has the same
  minimisers.
\item
  C15 says that certifying
  \texttt{P\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}1} over
  \texttt{G\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}(\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{})} is
  minimum-weight coset decoding, which the source calls NP-hard in
  general; the carriers here are small and declared, and no hardness
  statement about them is made or computed. The lemma
  \texttt{t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s}
  belongs to the separate Majorana package
  (\texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}F\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}9\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n}),
  not to source 212. It establishes only that the product of two
  declared positive natural-number parameters is positive
  (\texttt{N\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}s})
  and is not a formal leakage result.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{What stays outside.} C1 is a definition, and C5, C6, C8, C9, C10
and C17 remain fences. No device, capacitance, topological phase,
Pfaffian sign structure, fermion sign problem or vendor result is
touched by any computation here.

Found during the port and fixed after it. Each fix refuses bad input
with a typed error or computes what it names, and has a test that fails
on the old code.

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{QM\_120} ---

  \texttt{R\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}t}:
  it searches up to 16 observables and refuses unpaired, malformed and

  declared flag.
  \texttt{M\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}P\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}B\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e}

\subsection{5. Detailed implementation and reproduction
record}\label{detailed-implementation-and-reproduction-record}

This section records how selected finite certificates can be reproduced.
The software properties described here are not substitutes for the
mathematical arguments in §4 of this supplement and main paper §13. The
Rust crate

\textbf{QM\_082 --- channels as stochastic kernels.} A channel's
classical shadow is a
\texttt{S\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}M\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p}.
Composition now runs past the \texttt{i\allowbreak{}6\allowbreak{}4}
ceiling: a composite entry with a 79-bit reduced denominator is exact,
where the old carrier could not hold it.

\textbf{QM\_080 --- trace-norm geometry and dual witnesses.} In the
tested case the exact trace distance contracts under an exact CPTP map:
depolarizing at
\texttt{p\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}=\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2}
takes
\texttt{½\allowbreak{}‖\allowbreak{}ρ\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}−\allowbreak{} \allowbreak{}σ\allowbreak{}‖\allowbreak{}₁}
from \texttt{1} to \texttt{1\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}2}. That is one
certified instance, not the data-processing inequality.

\texttt{k\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s},

and

The port's historical validation records describe the tests then
executed. This section does not assert a fresh run of every pre-existing
test. Current focused reproduction has the explicitly recorded scope;
code ownership alone does not promote a claim.

\subsection{6. Open implementation programme and supporting
files}\label{open-implementation-programme-and-supporting-files}

\subsubsection{13.9 The five next derivations, in priority
order}\label{the-five-next-derivations-in-priority-order}

These are programme targets, not completed general derivations or a new
success census. The classical-storage obstruction of main paper §13.7
advances the sufficient-record and premise-separation targets on a
supplied qubit model; it does not derive that model from native
histories. Their order follows the dependencies of the measurement
account.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\item
  \textbf{Native histories to an available positive operational
  algebra.} Start with one Genesis/S(n) history presentation and prove
  which questions its quotient preserves. Construct the chosen
  dagger\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}groupoid algebra and state exactly
  where scalars, a positive cone, composition and available effects
  enter. Compare a classical commutative realization and the coherent
  one on the same protected experiments. The target is a faithful finite
  bridge with a premise-minimality countermodel for each unearned
  quantum input, not an inference from a dimension count. Reuse the
  category, Lie, number-theory, linear-algebra and WDP owners; finite
  sign holonomy alone does not supply the entire complex phase
  structure.
\item
  \textbf{Born representation on an explicitly closed effect domain.}
  Extend the present four-effect tomography and finite frame checks to a
  precise additivity, noncontextuality, normalization and positivity
  theorem on the chosen domain. Prove a positive trace-one
  representation there, or exhibit a valid non-Born countermodel.
  Distinguish all effects from a finite probe set and projective rays
  from normalized vectors; state any scalar extension or regularity
  needed to enlarge the domain. Reuse the exact linear-algebra and
  quantum-physics owners and the scoped
  Gleason\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}Busch Lean fragments. Representation
  under these assumptions would still price, rather than derive, those
  assumptions from primitive difference.
\item
  \textbf{An instrument derived from a declared apparatus coupling and
  report.} Starting with admitted preparation,
  isometry\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}unitary and pointer data, derive
  the grouped outcome maps, their effects, disturbance, non-selective
  channel and null-sector refusals. Prove the diagram from interaction
  to protected record questions commutes, and compare distinct
  instruments with the same effects. Reuse the exact instrument, Kraus,
  conditioning and WDP packet owners. The target closes a finite
  apparatus-to-instrument splice; conditioning remains dependent on an
  obtained outcome.
\item
  \textbf{Stable, sufficient records under composition and limited
  control.} For one specified open-system dynamics and effect menu,
  derive a pointer record algebra and the least available completion
  needed for future reports. Prove explicit error bounds for a declared
  time horizon and a compatible multi-observer comparison. Include an
  erasure control and a noncommuting-observable counterexample. Reuse
  exact population shadows, trace-norm witnesses, finite report gluing
  and the cochain\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}closure owners. An
  unrestricted linear completion, a product residual or a small sampled
  defect alone cannot certify physical record availability or
  entanglement.
\item
  \textbf{Outcome-premise separation with a finite
  observer\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}eraser protocol.} Extend the
  example above to a record-preserving observer and an observer with
  coherent joint control. For each proposed event or relative-record
  premise, derive its probabilities, repeatability and
  compatible-history conditions on exactly that protocol. Retain the
  affine deterministic-label obstruction as a control and identify what
  enlarged carrier escapes its hypotheses. Reuse finite instruments,
  history descent, contextuality and probability owners. A finished
  result must distinguish experimentally different predictions from
  empirically equivalent interpretive choices; it must not present a
  simulation's selected branch as a derived ontology.
\end{enumerate}

\subsubsection{13.10 What supports this
account}\label{what-supports-this-account}

The instrument formulae and reversible example are finite algebra on
supplied quantum inputs. The factorization and midpoint arguments are
the explicit mathematical reasoning above. Existing exact Rust controls
include
\texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s}
and the conditioning test in
\texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s}
under the quantum-physics owner. Their scope is admitted
instrument\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}dilation identities, conditional
states, probabilities and refusal controls; these tests do not establish
every claim in this section. The broader
Weyl\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}Gleason reproduction uses a separately
dated audit and is not a fresh complete build in this edition. The
classical-storage proof is separate from the eight exact native tests in
\texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s}:
sharp and strict-margin fixtures, a
refined\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}zero-letter POVM, rectangular
retrieval, complex Choi orientation,
malformed\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}nonpositive refusals, a static
classical countermodel, and available-control failure of a
population-only report. They do not test unrestricted hidden-variable
ontologies or realize a laboratory protocol. The additional Lean results
have exactly the scope stated in main paper §13.8. No physical
record-selection law or completed primitive-to-QM derivation is
asserted. A suitable next result must retain its premises, a
protected-question contract and an independently replayable finite
witness or counterexample.

\subsection{7. Removed implementation-specific carrier
passages}\label{removed-implementation-specific-carrier-passages}

Retained as a historical record. Nothing below is asserted beyond main
paper §13.8; where the two differ, §13.8 governs.

\paragraph{13.8.1 Connection to Projection Obstruction and native
Genesis}\label{connection-to-projection-obstruction-and-native-genesis}

The three tests of main paper §13.8 (future-question sufficiency,
positive Bell gluing, central sectors and purification) belong to
distinct mathematical interfaces. Phase-sensitive readouts and minimal
report spaces concern sufficiency relative to declared future
experiments; the central-weight bounds concern extensions of states on
direct-sum matrix algebras. None of these statements selects the
underlying quantum state space. A detailed comparison is retained in the
local companion manuscript {[}12{]}.

The native construction now closes a declared finite reachable passage
carrier and identifies states exactly when all admitted continuations
have equal protected answers and equal availability. Explicit joint
operations either preserve paired local reports or return a
distinguishing continuation and a stable refinement. These constructions
implement a minimal report relative to that finite experiment; they do
not yet provide the positive observable algebra, complex scalars or
tensor composition of a quantum model. The native experiment guide
{[}26{]} states the source, implementation and Lean boundaries.

The native Bell experiment and Test 2 have different premises. Shared
positive preparation weights and local native responses construct a
Bell-local model. Changing those weights with the settings gives the
guide's full-support, no-signalling table with \(S=12/5\); its setting
dependence is explicit. Test 2's \(S=14/5\) instead has the supplied
quantum realization above. Both tables exclude a common positive local
extension, but only the latter is furnished here with quantum states and
measurements. Neither constructs those quantum operations from Genesis.

Reference {[}12{]}, §4.3.2, also separates partial-trace consistency
from product independence: true marginals and products of one-site
marginals each form a closed section, even when their difference is
nonzero. Its §7.4 in the local companion copy (version 6.9.18; {[}12{]}
does not list that section) concerns defects hidden by observer kernels;
Bell gluing additionally requires positivity across measurement
contexts. ``Local observer,'' ``local tomography,'' and Bell ``local
causality'' therefore carry separate hypotheses. Appendix E's premise
table records the remaining algebraic, composition and availability
assumptions, including the distinct roles of finite Weyl representations
and Gleason-type probability uniqueness. The first derivation target
below remains open at precisely that operational quantum realization
step.
