\textbf{Constructive Weyl equivalence (written proof).} Let
\(K\subseteq\mathbb C\) be closed under conjugation and contain a
primitive \(N\)th root \(\omega\). Supply unitary \(N\times N\) matrices
\(X',Z'\) over \(K\) satisfying \(Z'X'=\omega X'Z'\) and \((X')^N=I\),
and a vector \(v\in K^N\) with \(Z'v=v\) and \(v^\dagger v=1\). Then the
matrix with columns \(v,X'v,\ldots,(X')^{N-1}v\) is unitary and
intertwines the pair with the canonical shift and clock. Indeed these
columns have norm one and are \(Z'\)-eigenvectors with the distinct
eigenvalues \(1,\omega,\ldots,\omega^{N-1}\). Unitary \(Z'\) makes
distinct eigenvectors orthogonal, and \((X')^N=I\) closes the last shift
column. These facts give both intertwining equations. An operator
commuting with the canonical clock is diagonal, because its eigenvalues
are distinct; commuting also with the shift makes that diagonal
constant. Two unitary intertwiners therefore differ only by a unit
scalar.

The reusable implementation is
\texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}W\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}H\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}:\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}k\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d}.
It checks the premises and both
unitary\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}intertwining equations exactly; its
test
\texttt{w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s}
(\texttt{o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}/}
in the repository) includes dimensions three and six and malformed
seed\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}period controls.
\texttt{W\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}C\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n}
establishes the dimension-independent entrywise scalar-commutant lemma
with distinct clock values and adjacent diagonal equalities supplied.
\texttt{H\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}4\allowbreak{}7} establishes integer
trace identities at dimensions two and three and an Eisenstein
three-dimensional Weyl fixture. Neither Lean module establishes the full
classification of irreducible representations or the existence of a
normalized seed over arbitrary \(K\).

\subparagraph{Target 20 (Loop 20): Quantum Error Mitigation via
Richardson Zero-Noise
Extrapolation}\label{target-20-loop-20-quantum-error-mitigation-via-richardson-zero-noise-extrapolation}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Mathematical Specification \& Operators:} Zero-Noise
  Extrapolation (ZNE) estimates an unmitigated expectation value
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle E_0 = \lim_{\lambda \to 0} E(\lambda)\)}\]
  from measurements collected at amplified noise scales
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \lambda_0 < \lambda_1 < \dots < \lambda_M\)}\].
  Assuming a polynomial noise response model
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle E(\lambda) = E_0 + \sum_{k=1}^M c_k \lambda^k + \mathcal{O}(\lambda^{M+1})\)}\],
  the Richardson estimator is
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \widehat{E}_0 = \sum_{j=0}^M \gamma_j E(\lambda_j).\)}\]
  The extrapolation weights \(\gamma \in \mathbb{Q}^{M+1}\) are
  determined by the exact Vandermonde linear system:
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \sum_{j=0}^M \gamma_j = 1, \qquad \sum_{j=0}^M \gamma_j \lambda_j^k = 0 \quad \text{for } k \in \{1, \dots, M\}.\)}\]
  For uniform integer noise scale factors \(\lambda_j = j + 1\):

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    Linear extrapolation (\(M=1\), scales \(\{1, 2\}\)):
    \(\gamma = (2, -1)\).
  \item
    Quadratic extrapolation (\(M=2\), scales \(\{1, 2, 3\}\)):
    \(\gamma = (3, -3, 1)\).
  \item
    Cubic extrapolation (\(M=3\), scales \(\{1, 2, 3, 4\}\)):
    \(\gamma = (4, -6, 4, -1)\).
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Discrete Carrier:} Exact rational field \(\mathbb{Q}\),
  integer weight vectors \(\mathbb{Z}^{M+1}\), discrete noise scale
  lattice.
\item
  \textbf{Invariants \& Algebraic Relations:}

  \begin{enumerate}
  \def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
  \tightlist
  \item
    Weight normalization: \(\sum_{j=0}^M \gamma_j = 1\).
  \item
    Noise moment nullification:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \sum_{j=0}^M \gamma_j \lambda_j^k = 0\)}\]
    for all \(1 \le k \le M\).
  \item
    Exact reconstruction: for any noisy polynomial model of degree
    \(\le M\),
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \sum_{j=0}^M \gamma_j E(\lambda_j) = E_0\)}\]
    identically without residual bias.
  \item
    Extrapolation coefficient 1-norm and variance overhead:
    \(\|\gamma\|_1=2^{M+1}-1\) for these equally spaced scales, giving
    \(3,7,15\). If independent sample means each have variance \(v\),
    the estimator variance is \(v\sum_j\gamma_j^2\), giving
    \(5v,19v,69v\). If instead each shot has variance \(\sigma^2\) and
    \(N\) shots are shared optimally with continuous allocation
    \(n_j\propto|\gamma_j|\), the minimum is
    \(\sigma^2\|\gamma\|_1^2/N\), giving factors \(9,49,225\) relative
    to \(\sigma^2/N\). Integer allocation and unequal per-scale
    variances require their own budget calculation.
  \end{enumerate}
\item
  \textbf{Cross-References:}

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    Python:
    \texttt{p\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}y}
    (\texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s},
    \texttt{r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}z\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e},
    \texttt{s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}x\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n}).

    (\texttt{l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}w\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}m},
    \texttt{l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d},
    \texttt{l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n},

\subparagraph{Target 21 (Loop 21): Discrete Quantum Walk on Permutation
Group Cayley
Graphs}\label{target-21-loop-21-discrete-quantum-walk-on-permutation-group-cayley-graphs}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Mathematical Specification \& Operators:} A discrete-time
  quantum walk (DTQW) on a regular directed graph \(G = (V, E)\)
  operates on the tensor space
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \mathcal{H} = \mathcal{H}_{\text{coin}} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\text{position}}\)}\].
  The evolution operator per time step is \(U = S (C \otimes I_V)\),
  where \(C\) is a unitary coin operator (e.g.~Hadamard or Grover
  diffusion) on \(\mathcal{H}_{\text{coin}}\) and \(S\) is the position
  shift operator
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle S |c, v\rangle = |c, v \cdot g_c\rangle\)}\]
  determined by generator \(g_c\). We evaluate Cayley graphs of finite
  symmetric groups generated by Coxeter generators (adjacent
  transpositions \(s_i = (i, i+1)\)):

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Cay}(S_3, \{s_1, s_2\})\)}\]:
    order \(|S_3| = 6\), degree 2, diameter \(D=3\).
  \item
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Cay}(S_4, \{s_1, s_2, s_3\})\)}\]:
    order \(|S_4| = 24\), degree 3, diameter \(D=6\).
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Discrete Carrier:} Finite symmetric groups \(S_3, S_4\),
  Coxeter generators, integer distance distributions, discrete graph
  coin-shift unitary algebra.
\item
  \textbf{Invariants \& Algebraic Relations:}

  \begin{enumerate}
  \def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
  \tightlist
  \item
    Exact distance distribution / Poincaré polynomial:

    \begin{itemize}
    \tightlist
    \item
      For \(S_3\), distance distribution from identity is
      \((1, 2, 2, 1)\), summing to \(|S_3| = 6\), with diameter \(D=3\).
    \item
      For \(S_4\), distance distribution is \((1, 3, 5, 6, 5, 3, 1)\),
      summing to \(|S_4| = 24\), matching the Poincaré polynomial
      \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle P_{S_4}(q) = (1+q)(1+q+q^2)(1+q+q^2+q^3)\)}\],
      with diameter \(D=6\).
    \end{itemize}
  \item
    Finite propagation: for a state initially at the identity, position
    support satisfies \(d_{\text{front}}(t)\le\min(t,D)\). Equality
    requires a specified coin and initial coin state; with the identity
    coin and one occupied involutory generator, the walker returns at
    step two and the front is zero.
  \item
    The distance variance is bounded by \(D^2/4\) at every time. The
    formal envelope \(\min(t,D)\) alone does not prove ballistic spread
    of an evolved state. The cited \(S_4\) module checks its actual walk
    only at steps 0, 1 and 2.
  \item
    For the declared \(S_3\) fixture, nonzero amplitude reaches the
    longest word \(w_0=s_1s_2s_1\) at step three; this is a fixture
    result, not a coin-independent law.
  \end{enumerate}
\item
  \textbf{Cross-References:}

\subparagraph{\texorpdfstring{Target 22 (Loop 22): Discrete Mutually
Unbiased Basis (MUB) State Tomography in Dimension
\(d=3\)}{Target 22 (Loop 22): Discrete Mutually Unbiased Basis (MUB) State Tomography in Dimension d=3}}\label{target-22-loop-22-discrete-mutually-unbiased-basis-mub-state-tomography-in-dimension-d3}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Mathematical Specification \& Operators:} In prime dimension
  \(d=3\), there exist \(d + 1 = 4\) mutually unbiased bases (MUBs)
  \(\{B_0, B_1, B_2, B_3\}\), each consisting of \(d=3\) orthonormal
  states, providing \(d(d+1) = 12\) rank-1 projection operators
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \Pi_{b, j} = |v_{b, j}\rangle\langle v_{b, j}|\)}\]:

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    \(B_0\): Computational basis
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \{|0\rangle, |1\rangle, |2\rangle\}\)}\].
  \item
    \(B_1\): Discrete Fourier basis (eigenbasis of shift operator
    \(X\)).
  \item
    \(B_2\): Eigenbasis of \(X Z\).
  \item
    \(B_3\): Eigenbasis of \(X Z^2\). Within each basis, projectors are
    mutually orthogonal:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_{b, j} \Pi_{b, k}) = \delta_{j, k}\)}\].
    Across different bases, projectors have constant mutual overlap:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_{b, j} \Pi_{b', k}) = \frac{1}{d} = \frac{1}{3} \quad (\text{for } b \ne b').\)}\]
    For any density operator \(\rho \in M_3(\mathbb{C})\), measurement
    probabilities are
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle p_{b, j} = \operatorname{Tr}(\rho \Pi_{b, j})\)}\].
    The density matrix is reconstructed via the exact rational linear
    inversion formula:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \rho = \sum_{b=0}^3 \sum_{j=0}^2 p_{b, j} \Pi_{b, j} - I_3.\)}\]
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Discrete Carrier:} Eisenstein cyclotomic field
  \(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_3)\) (minimal polynomial \(x^2 + x + 1 = 0\))
  embedded in \(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{24})\), ring of integers
  \(\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_3]\), exact rational arithmetic \(\mathbb{Q}\).
\item
  \textbf{Invariants \& Algebraic Relations:}

  \begin{enumerate}
  \def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
  \tightlist
  \item
    Orthonormality within basis:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_{b, j} \Pi_{b, k}) = \delta_{j, k}\)}\].
  \item
    Unbiasedness across bases:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_{b, j} \Pi_{b', k}) = 1/3\)}\]
    for \(b \ne b'\).
  \item
    Projector resolution: \(\sum_{j=0}^2 \Pi_{b, j} = I_3\) for each
    basis \(b \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}\).
  \item
    Total sum identity:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \sum_{b=0}^3 \sum_{j=0}^2 \Pi_{b, j} = 4 I_3 = (d+1) I_d\)}\].
  \item
    Exact tomography inversion identity: for any state \(\rho\),
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}\left(\left(\sum_{b, j} p_{b, j} \Pi_{b, j} - I_3\right) \Pi_{\beta, \mu}\right) = p_{\beta, \mu}\)}\],
    establishing exact state recovery without information loss.
  \end{enumerate}
\item
  \textbf{Cross-References:}

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    Python:
    \texttt{p\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}q\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}y}
    (\texttt{b\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}j\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s},
    \texttt{r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s},

    \texttt{v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}f\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}s},
    an alias of

  \item
    Rust:
    \texttt{n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}v\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s}
    (\texttt{c\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}3\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}y});
    \texttt{m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s},

    and
    \texttt{c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s}
    are former
    \texttt{c\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s}
    labels.
  \item
    Lean 4:

    (\texttt{m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}m\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}g},
    \texttt{m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}1},
    \texttt{m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}0\allowbreak{}2},
    \texttt{m\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}b\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}h\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}1\allowbreak{}2},

\subparagraph{\texorpdfstring{Target 22 Extension: Galois Field
\(\mathbb{F}_4\) and 5 MUBs in Dimension \(d=4\)
(Positive-Reconstruction
Obstruction)}{Target 22 Extension: Galois Field \textbackslash mathbb\{F\}\_4 and 5 MUBs in Dimension d=4 (Positive-Reconstruction Obstruction)}}\label{target-22-extension-galois-field-mathbbf_4-and-5-mubs-in-dimension-d4-positive-reconstruction-obstruction}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Mathematical Specification \& Operators:} In prime-power
  dimension \(d = 2^2 = 4\) (two qubits), the maximal set of
  \(d + 1 = 5\) mutually unbiased bases \(\{B_0, B_1, B_2, B_3, B_4\}\)
  is constructed from the 5 maximal abelian subalgebras (MASAs) of the
  2-qubit Pauli group \(P_2 / Z(P_2)\), corresponding to the 5 isotropic
  lines of the symplectic spread in
  \(\mathbb{F}_4 \times \mathbb{F}_4\):

  \begin{itemize}
  \tightlist
  \item
    MASA 0:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \{Z \otimes I, I \otimes Z, Z \otimes Z\}\)}\]
    (computational basis)
  \item
    MASA 1:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \{X \otimes I, I \otimes X, X \otimes X\}\)}\]
    (Hadamard-dual basis)
  \item
    MASA 2:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \{Y \otimes I, I \otimes Y, Y \otimes Y\}\)}\]
    (phase basis)
  \item
    MASA 3:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \{X \otimes Y, Y \otimes Z, Z \otimes X\}\)}\]
    (entangled cyclic MASA A)
  \item
    MASA 4:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \{X \otimes Z, Y \otimes X, Z \otimes Y\}\)}\]
    (entangled cyclic MASA B) Each MASA yields 4 simultaneous orthogonal
    rank-1 projectors
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \Pi(s_0, s_1) = \frac{1}{4}(I_4 + s_0 M_0)(I_4 + s_1 M_1)\)}\]
    for \(s_0, s_1 \in \{+1, -1\}\), providing 20 rank-1 projectors
    total. For any state \(\rho\), the exact rational linear inversion
    formula reconstructs \(\rho\):
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \rho = \sum_{b=0}^4 \sum_{j=0}^3 p_{b, j} \Pi_{b, j} - I_4.\)}\]
  \end{itemize}
\item
  \textbf{Discrete Carrier:} Gaussian cyclotomic field
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \mathbb{Q}(i) = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_4)\)}\]
  embedded in \(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{24})\), ring of integers
  \(\mathbb{Z}[i]\), Galois field
  \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \mathbb{F}_4 \cong \mathbb{F}_2[x]/(x^2 + x + 1)\)}\],
  and exact rational arithmetic \(\mathbb{Q}\).
\item
  \textbf{Invariants \& Algebraic Relations:}

  \begin{enumerate}
  \def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
  \tightlist
  \item
    Orthonormality within basis:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_{b, j} \Pi_{b, k}) = \delta_{j, k}\)}\]
    for all \(b \in \{0, \dots, 4\}\).
  \item
    Unbiasedness across bases:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_{b, j} \Pi_{b', k}) = 1/4\)}\]
    for all \(b \ne b'\).
  \item
    Total sum identity:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \sum_{b=0}^4 \sum_{j=0}^3 \Pi_{b, j} = 5 I_4 = (d+1) I_d\)}\].
  \item
    Trace preservation: for any valuation or probability assignment,
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}(\rho) = \sum_{b=0}^4 (1) - 4 = 1\)}\].
  \item
    Entangled state tomography: linear inversion reconstructs the
    entangled Bell state
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle |\Phi^+\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|00\rangle + |11\rangle)\)}\]
    with machine fidelity (\(F = 1.000000\), error
    \(< 2 \times 10^{-15}\)).
  \item
    Valuation reconstruction obstruction: for any deterministic
    assignment \(v\in\{0,1,2,3\}^5\) choosing one projector per basis,
    the linearly reconstructed trace-one operator has exact squared
    trace:
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}(\rho(v)^2) = 5(1) + 20(1/4) - 2(5) + 4 = 4 > 1.\)}\]
    Because physical density matrices satisfy
    \[\protect\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Tr}(\rho^2) \le (\operatorname{Tr}\rho)^2 = 1\)}\],
    a purity of 4 algebraically forces at least one eigenvalue to be
    negative.
  \item
    Numerical demonstration: in floating point, all \(4^5 = 1,024\)
    extreme vertices have \(\lambda_{\min}(v) \le -1/2\) (minimum
    \(\approx -0.8968\)); the exact argument is item 6.
  \item
    For a complete set of \(d+1\) MUBs the same calculation gives
    \(\operatorname{Tr}(\rho(v)^2)=d\), hence excess \(d-1\): one at
    \(d=2\), two at \(d=3\) and three at \(d=4\). This excludes
    representing each deterministic assignment by a positive quantum
    state. It does not exclude a classical joint distribution for these
    separate basis measurements: \(\mu(v)=\prod_b p_b(v_b)\) reproduces
    any declared basis marginals. A contextuality no-go needs additional
    shared-context or operational constraints.
  \end{enumerate}

The public archive holds all 67 current original manuscripts under
\texttt{s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/}.
Every subsection 11.N of §4 links its corresponding ZIP-local paper.
Those links are the public source index: a reader can move from a
consolidated result directly to the original manuscript in the same
archive. The receipted Lean rows and retained fixtures continue to cite
the version against which they were actually checked. Six historical
package snapshots remain under repository custody but are not part of
the public ZIP. Repository tests check current originals and retained
copies separately and reject unrecorded changes. Five retained copies
differ from their historical disposition digests. The 2026-10-13
semantic reconciliation permits current claim use by assessing each
pinned version and binding its corrected downstream statements. It does
not declare the bytes identical or erase the historical disposition. In
particular, the new zero-centered dual proposed in the retained channel
paper is rejected; the correct spectral-diameter dual in §11.35 of this
supplement remains in force. Source archives are preserved.
\texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}i\allowbreak{}n\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}d\allowbreak{}\_\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}o\allowbreak{}u\allowbreak{}r\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}p\allowbreak{}y}
binds the 37 superposition-paper and 336 finite-Hilbert-boundary
snapshot files to the earlier checked-in catalog, without requiring
equality to the evolving originals or silently skipping an absent
source.

For each unresolved mathematical statement:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  state its domain, quantifiers, assumptions, and conclusion precisely;
\item
  supply an adequate written proof, a matching formal proof, or a
  complete exact finite argument appropriate to those quantifiers;
\item
  otherwise restrict the statement, identify it as open, or withdraw it;
  and
\item
  record any example test only as evidence about its stated inputs.
\end{enumerate}

The repository-only evidence record tracks provenance and reproduction.
Its status transitions do not determine whether the mathematical
obligation has been discharged.

\texttt{t\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}t\allowbreak{}s\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}l\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}g\allowbreak{}a\allowbreak{}c\allowbreak{}y\allowbreak{}/\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}2\allowbreak{}e\allowbreak{}/}
contains the historical model-integration suite. Its old execution
counts describe their recorded revisions. The reference engines consume
the declared cochain packet directly, so an executable sequence exists.
The derivation problem remains open because the packet, scalar field,
readout, composition and physical interpretation still need justified
bridges.
